artigo.texto: Samsung em negociações para adquirir a fabricante de sistemas de resfriamento para data centers Modine; MOD dispara mais de 25% no pré-mercado A Samsung Electronics negocia a aquisição da fabricante norte-americana Modine Manufacturing, impulsionada pelo crescimento na demanda por resfriamento de data centers de IA. A notícia elevou as ações da Modine em mais de 25% no pré-mercado. A divisão de data centers da Modine registrou receita de US$ 440 milhões, alta de 95% no trimestre encerrado em setembro. Para a Samsung, a aquisição diversificaria receitas além dos chips de memória, expandindo sua atuação em infraestrutura de IA e fortalecendo sua posição no mercado norte-americano, complementando investimentos anteriores no setor de gerenciamento térmico. TradingKey - A Samsung Electronics está em negociações com a fabricante norte-americana de equipamentos de resfriamento para data centers Modine Manufacturing sobre um potencial acordo de aquisição que pode ser selado já nas próximas semanas, informou a Bloomberg, citando pessoas a par do assunto. Após a notícia, as ações da Modine Manufacturing (MOD) dispararam mais de 25% no pré-mercado de sexta-feira. Fonte: TradingView Nenhuma das partes tomou uma decisão final, as negociações ainda podem fracassar e o surgimento de outros interessados não pode ser descartado. Tanto a Samsung Electronics quanto a Modine Manufacturing se recusaram a comentar as notícias. O surgimento da Modine Manufacturing como potencial alvo de aquisição é impulsionado principalmente pelo rápido crescimento da demanda por resfriamento em data centers de inteligência artificial. À medida que o consumo de energia e a densidade dos racks de servidores de IA continuam aumentando, os equipamentos tradicionais de resfriamento a ar enfrentam dificuldades para atender aos requisitos de dissipação térmica de alguns grandes data centers, elevando a importância de chillers, sistemas de resfriamento líquido e outras soluções de gerenciamento térmico de alta eficiência. Atualmente, a Modine Manufacturing fornece esses equipamentos para clientes de nuvem de hiperescala na América do Norte, e seu negócio de data centers se tornou o segmento de crescimento mais rápido da empresa. No trimestre encerrado no fim de setembro, a receita da Modine Manufacturing com data centers atingiu US$ 440 milhões, alta de 95% na comparação anual, enquanto o lucro operacional cresceu 70%, para US$ 61,2 milhões. Impactada pelo aumento dos custos de materiais, componentes e tarifas, a margem bruta do segmento recuou 4,7 pontos percentuais, para 19,7%, embora os pedidos e a carteira de pedidos tenham permanecido fortes. A empresa projeta que, excluindo os negócios cindidos, a receita principal no ano fiscal de 2027 crescerá entre 50% e 55% em relação ao ano anterior. A Modine Manufacturing concluiu a cisão de seu negócio de Performance Technologies em outubro e o fundiu com a Gentherm. Após a reestruturação, a empresa manteve suas operações de data centers e HVAC comercial, aprofundando ainda mais seu foco operacional em mercados de gerenciamento térmico de alto crescimento. A companhia também recebeu uma distribuição em dinheiro de aproximadamente US$ 156 milhões, utilizada para amortizar dívidas. Estruturalmente, a Modine Manufacturing transformou-se de uma fornecedora diversificada de componentes industriais em uma empresa puramente focada em soluções de resfriamento e climatização para data centers, o que também ampliou sua atratividade como alvo de M&A. Para a Samsung, a potencial aquisição traria uma nova fonte de receita com data centers além dos chips de memória. Embora a Samsung gere um fluxo de caixa substancial a partir de sua divisão de memórias, sua lucratividade permanece vulnerável aos ciclos de preços dos chips. Combinar chips para servidores e produtos de armazenamento com equipamentos de gerenciamento térmico para data centers ajudaria a companhia a expandir sua presença no mercado de infraestrutura de IA e a diminuir sua dependência de um único negócio. A Samsung já fortaleceu competências correlatas anteriormente por meio de aquisições. Em 2025, a empresa desembolsou 1,5 bilhão de euros para adquirir a alemã de HVAC FläktGroup, ampliando suas soluções de resfriamento para data centers. A compra da Modine Manufacturing proporcionaria à Samsung relacionamentos adicionais com clientes na América do Norte, instalações industriais e produtos de resfriamento de alta potência, com potencial para acelerar sinergias com seus próprios negócios de semicondutores e servidores. artigo.texto: Europe is expected to have sufficient electricity resources to meet demand during the winter of 2026–2027, although some areas could face supply risks, particularly those with limited or no interconnection to the continental European network, according to the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity (ENTSO-E). Its Winter Outlook 2026–2027 identifies Cyprus as the area with the most notable risks, while also detecting potential adequacy concerns in Malta, Ireland, eastern Denmark, Finland and Northern Ireland. Compared with the previous winter, Europe's installed renewable energy capacity has increased by approximately 134 GW, or 16%, mainly driven by solar photovoltaic and wind power. Solar capacity grew by 26%, adding 96 GW, while wind capacity rose by 13%, equivalent to 33 GW. Battery energy storage capacity more than doubled, increasing by over 124% to reach 38 GW. Meanwhile, installed hard coal and lignite capacity declined by nearly 6 GW, or 9%, and gas-fired capacity fell by almost 9 GW, or 5%. Despite the overall favourable outlook, ENTSO-E identifies different levels of risk across several electricity systems. Cyprus faces potential supply risks due to its lack of interconnection with the continental European network. In Malta and Ireland, some risks appear under normal market conditions, although dedicated non-market resources significantly reduce them. The report also identifies signs of expected energy not served and adequacy risks in eastern Denmark (DK2), Finland and Northern Ireland. Ukraine and Moldova face higher risks for the coming winter. According to the report, Ukraine's electricity supply situation remains uncertain because of potential attacks on energy infrastructure. Moldova, meanwhile, is exposed to several vulnerabilities, including its strong dependence on electricity imports from Romania through a single Isaccea–Vulcanesti interconnector, insufficient net transfer capacity allocated for commercial trading to cover its electricity deficit, and potential disruptions in the Ukrainian power system linked to Russia's war of aggression. ENTSO-E also notes that planned generation outages are slightly higher than last winter, mainly due to increased planned maintenance outages at French nuclear plants. Electricity demand is also slightly higher, while hydro reservoir levels are below average overall. The assessment adds that some European countries could need to rely on imports during periods of low renewable generation and limited conventional generation availability. Cross-border cooperation and coordination between transmission system operators (TSOs) will therefore be essential to maintain the balance between electricity supply and demand throughout the winter. ENTSO-E highlights the role of weekly operational coordination between TSOs and regional coordination centres, alongside national Risk Preparedness Plans and regional processes designed to identify and address potential shortages. The organisation stresses that the Winter Outlook is not a forecast, but an assessment of potential resource adequacy risks based on reference scenarios and different sensitivities. Actual conditions could become tighter if demand, weather, generation availability or cross-border electricity exchanges differ from the assumptions used in the analysis. European TSOs will continue to monitor supply adequacy throughout the winter.

artigo.texto: Trailer-Mounted Battery Storage System Offers Up to 1.84 MWh of Mobile Capacity A trailer-mounted battery energy storage system (BESS) offers up to 1.84 MWh of storage capacity for construction sites, utility emergency response, remote industrial operations and other applications requiring temporary or mobile power. Soneil Spark's Mobile Battery Energy Storage System integrates lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries and power controls into a towable trailer. Standard configurations range from 230 kWh to 920 kWh, with custom systems available up to 1,840 kWh. Power output ranges from 115 kW to 460 kW, with custom configurations reaching 920 kW. The system is designed to provide power at locations where permanent electrical service is unavailable or where temporary power requirements make conventional installations impractical. Potential applications include construction sites awaiting utility connections, utility storm restoration, outdoor events, film production, and remote mining and agricultural operations. The Mobile BESS can operate with grid power, generators or solar generation. Its hybrid operating capabilities include peak shaving, generator synchronization and grid export, subject to utility approval. When paired with generators, the battery system can supply power during periods of peak demand and equipment startup, potentially reducing generator runtime and fuel consumption. The trailer-mounted design is intended to provide greater mobility than conventional containerized energy storage systems. Features include independent air suspension to reduce vibration during transport, all-terrain tires and ground clearance ranging from 6 to 14 inches. The system uses LFP battery chemistry rated for more than 8,000 cycles. Standard operating temperatures range from -20 C to 50 C, with an optional cold-weather configuration extending the lower operating limit to -35 C. Safety features include automatic fire suppression at both the battery and trailer levels. The system lists UL 1973, UN 38.3 and UL 1741 standards and is designed to meet UL 9540A requirements. LTE-based remote monitoring provides real-time alerts and remote diagnostics. The system also includes a two-year warranty and 24/7 technical support. An optional configuration incorporates electric vehicle charging. Soneil Spark, based in Brampton, Ontario, will demonstrate the Mobile BESS at RE+ 2026, Nov. 17–19, in Las Vegas.

artigo.texto: Chile reached 3,125 MW and 13,555 MWh of operational energy storage by the end of September 2026 , practically double the capacity recorded at the end of last year. However, the growth of battery storage raises questions about the ability of regulatory instruments to support the transformation of the electricity system, a discussion that Generadoras de Chile brought before the National Energy Commission (CNE) during the recent review of peak pricing controls. “ We are raising a fundamental question: whether traditional peak control mechanisms continue to provide efficient signals for a system whose demand, generation, and storage availability change significantly over time ,” said Camilo Charme , executive director of Generadoras de Chile, in an interview with Energía Estratégica . The controversy arose after the National Energy Commission (CNE) approved, through Exempt Resolution No. 513 of September 17, the preliminary technical report on the methodology for determining peak demand control periods. The public comment period concluded on October 29, allowing stakeholders in the sector to submit proposals regarding the criteria used to identify periods of peak electricity demand. In that context, Generadoras requested the incorporation of a better representation of critical scenarios, operational restrictions, effective availability of resources and demand response , in addition to strengthening the transparency of the indicators used. “ Beyond perfecting the current methodology, we propose evaluating alternatives that link economic signals with the actual risks of insufficiency, considering consumer behavior and the expected evolution of the system ,” Charme said. More than 8000 MW of BESS are progressing between testing and construction The growth of energy storage infrastructure is far from slowing down. According to the latest statistics from the Chilean Renewable Energy and Storage Association (ACERA) , Chile has 3,017 MW of battery storage capacity undergoing testing and another 5,130 MW under construction , representing more than 8,100 MW in various stages prior to commercial operation. The prominence of this technology is also reflected in its energy contribution. During September, BESS systems injected 584 GWh into the National Electric System , equivalent to 7.9% of the injections recorded by technology and 216.3% more than in the same month of 2025. However, the increase in installed capacity still faces significant limitations in harnessing renewable energy generation. Between January and September, solar and wind power curtailments totaled 3,546 GWh , although this represents a year-on-year decrease of 4.6%. This situation demonstrates that battery availability alone does not solve the infrastructure and operational problems of the grid. Continue reading In addition to the technical challenges, new economic pressures are emerging. During the Future Energy Summit Chile 2026 , representatives from Atlas Renewable Energy and DNV warned that increasing competition among BESS projects is reducing energy arbitrage margins and leading financial institutions to demand more rigorous profitability assessments. This scenario broadens the discussion on how to remunerate the services that batteries can provide, beyond simply transferring energy between schedules. Power availability, discharge duration, and contingency response become relevant for evaluating their effective contribution to the security and sufficiency of supply —two aspects that Generadoras de Chile considers necessary to incorporate into future economic signals. Power generators demand changes in dispatch and remuneration In this context, the association is also working on determining the opportunity cost of storage, its operational scheduling, and price formation. These proposals are part of a wholesale market reform agenda that goes beyond the specific review of peak pricing controls. “ Chile must gradually move towards a competitive bidding market, incorporating pre-day and intraday trading mechanisms, where different agents can reveal the value of their resources and properly manage their risks ,” Charme said. Currently, the National Electric Coordinator manages dispatch under a cost-based scheme. The evolution proposed by the industry association would involve introducing additional commercial tools to recognize the value of available resources over different time horizons, with requirements for transparency and competition oversight. The initiative is part of ongoing work that Generadoras has been developing in conjunction with the authorities. On September 5 , the organization submitted technical studies to the CNE (National Energy Commission) on energy storage, security, grid robustness, and complementary services, in addition to sharing updates on its proposals for bidding markets. Among the short-term priorities is the updating of the Technical Standard for Coordination and Operation , a process for which the authority appointed a Special Advisory Committee in September. The discussion includes aspects related to the integration of new technologies and the efficiency of the services necessary to maintain electrical stability. According to the industry, the modifications must take into account the conditions that the country will face in the coming years, anticipating both the required investments and the availability of essential capabilities to respond to contingencies. “ It is not enough to verify that the current mechanisms function under known conditions. We must assess how they will respond to the future configuration of the system, anticipating the capabilities, investments, and adjustments necessary to maintain a safe and reliable supply ,” Charme concluded.

artigo.texto: Data centers devem atrair R$ 1 tri até 2036 e estimular térmicas no Brasil Alto consumo de energia desses projetos demanda estrutura complementar às fontes renováveis, apontam especialistas A combinação entre alta demanda de processamento de dados pela inteligência artificial (IA), incentivos fiscais e a oferta de energia renovável tem o potencial de atrair para o Brasil até R$ 1 trilhão em investimentos em data centers nos próximos dez anos. A estimativa é da Associação Brasileira de Data Center (ABDC), que avaliou o impacto das desonerações para o setor previstas no programa federal Redata. No entanto, especialistas afirmam que a atração de projetos desse tipo deve estimular também novos empreendimentos de geração de energia, particularmente termelétricas movidas a gás natural. - O preço da ‘ressaca digital’: quanto custou ao mundo a pane global do Outlook da Microsoft? - Nvidia: entenda por que escândalo que derrubou CEO acirra disputa entre EUA e China por chips de IA Embora as fontes renováveis devam ter papel importante no atendimento à demanda energética desses grandes galpões recheados de servidores, especialistas e técnicos do governo apontam a necessidade de reforçar o sistema elétrico para dar estabilidade a esse fornecimento. Isso porque termelétricas podem funcionar continuamente, preenchendo lacunas deixadas, por exemplo, pelas gerações eólica e solar, que são sujeitas ao clima. A modalidade também é acionada quando hidrelétricas têm reservatórios limitados por estiagens. No entanto, usinas a gás são mais caras e poluentes. De acordo com a Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), os data centers serão um dos principais vetores de crescimento do consumo de energia no Brasil na próxima década. Com o crescimento médio anual de 13,7% na demanda por eletricidade esperado até 2036, o segmento deve responder por cerca de 3% da demanda total do país até lá, algo em torno de 30 bilhões de kWh. É o suficiente para atender quase 14 milhões de residências durante um ano. Nesse cenário, a geração termelétrica a gás natural é vista hoje pela EPE como uma das principais alternativas para atender às necessidades futuras do sistema em termos de potência, flexibilidade na operação e segurança de suprimento. A estatal estima que os investimentos em termelétricas a gás deverão somar R$ 12,45 bilhões em uma década no país. “No curto e médio prazos, o gás aparece como um recurso relevante para fornecer os atributos que um sistema cada vez mais renovável necessita”, atesta a EPE, destacando a importância de projetos capazes de mitigar as emissões das termelétricas como iniciativas de captura e armazenamento de carbono. - Escândalo da Nvidia: 'Culto ao fundador' moldou o Vale do Silício e põe em xeque futuro da empresa Luis Tossi, vice-presidente da ABDC, concorda que é necessário garantir segurança e confiabilidade ao sistema elétrico para consolidar a atração de data centers, o que passa também por investir na expansão de linhas de transmissão para aproveitar melhor a geração renovável: — O Redata é uma das medidas para criar condições mais competitivas para que o Brasil participe da expansão global da infraestrutura digital, especialmente diante do crescimento da IA. Isso não significa que o Brasil absorverá toda essa demanda mundial. O tamanho da parcela que conseguiremos atrair dependerá de diferentes fatores, e um dos principais será nossa capacidade de disponibilizar energia e infraestrutura para conectar esses novos empreendimentos. Capacidade em expansão Segundo a EPE, a previsão é que entrem no sistema 11.124 MW de novas usinas termelétricas a gás natural, com entrada em operação a partir de 2028. Além dessa capacidade já contratada, o Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia (PDE) 2036, elaborado pela instituição, indica outros 2.798 MW de expansão termelétrica não renovável, sendo aproximadamente 1.396 MW de novas térmicas flexíveis a gás e 1.403 MW por meio de recondicionamento de usinas existentes. “À medida que cresce a participação de fontes renováveis variáveis, o sistema não necessita apenas de mais energia, mas também de recursos capazes de fornecer potência e flexibilidade quando necessário”, afirmou a EPE em nota enviada ao GLOBO. Apesar de o presidente Lula ter sancionado em setembro o Redata, que reduz impostos sobre importação e aquisição de equipamentos de empresas interessadas em instalar ou ampliar data centers no Brasil, o programa ainda precisa definir o alcance das fontes de energia que poderão usar usadas pelos data centers. Isso porque, na aprovação do texto, o Senado substituiu a expressão “energia limpa” por “energia de baixo carbono” para condicionar os benefícios. Procurada pelo GLOBO, a Casa Civil não informou quando vai publicar essa norma. Segundo Tossi, essa definição é importante para orientar as decisões dos investidores. Ele cita como alternativas os sistemas de baterias para armazenar energia para uso nos de menor oferta renovável: — O desafio é garantir que o sistema brasileiro tenha flexibilidade suficiente para combinar sua ampla disponibilidade de energia renovável com soluções capazes de assegurar o fornecimento contínuo exigido pela infraestrutura digital. O Brasil já fez os primeiros leilões de reserva de capacidade voltados a sistemas de armazenamento em baterias. É um avanço, mas não cabe ao setor de data centers estabelecer antecipadamente qual tecnologia deve substituir outra. Essa combinação dependerá da evolução dos custos, da escala dos projetos, da duração necessária do armazenamento e da regulamentação. Como os data centers precisam de energia firme 24 horas, é preciso complementar fontes como solar e eólica, que só geram cerca de 40% do tempo, avalia Edvaldo Santana, ex-diretor da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel): — Falar em data center com 100% de energia renovável não é verdade. Pode ser grande parte, mas não tudo. Temos um sistema integrado e vamos ter um cenário de mix de fontes, com hidrelétrica, térmica a gás, solar e eólica.

The global market for rheology additives for battery electrodes is positioned for robust expansion over the 2026-2035 forecast period, underpinned by the rapid scaling of lithium-ion battery production for electric vehicles and stationary storage. These specialized chemicals, including thickeners and viscosity modifiers, are essential for controlling slurry flow and coating uniformity during electrode manufacturing, directly influencing cell performance and yield. Additionally, fast-charging capabilities demand electrodes with tailored porosity and adhesion, further elevating the role of rheology control. artigo.texto: Cabot Corporation Major player in activated carbon for food & beverage According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Food Grade Activated Carbon market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global food grade activated carbon market is entering a phase of structural evolution rather than simple volume expansion. As a non-discretionary processing aid embedded in large-scale ingredient streams such as sugar, edible oils, and beverages, demand is anchored by regulatory compliance and core processing efficiency. However, the market is bifurcating between commoditized bulk decolorization and high-service specialty purification, where technical service, documentation rigor, and selective adsorption profiles command meaningful price premiums. Through 2035, growth will be concentrated in premium beverage processing, advanced water recycling and zero-liquid-discharge systems, and targeted contaminant removal, as food manufacturers seek to achieve clarity, taste, and stability without declaring artificial processing aids on labels. Supply security remains critically dependent on geographically concentrated feedstock streams, particularly coconut shell, making vertical integration and long-term sourcing agreements key competitive levers. Energy costs continue to pressure thermal activation and reactivation economics, forcing efficiency innovation. This report provides a structured, commercially grounded analysis of market size, segmentation, demand architecture, pricing, competitive positioning, and regional dynamics, with forward-looking scenarios through 2035. The baseline scenario for the food grade activated carbon market through 2035 assumes continued, moderate expansion supported by population growth, processed food consumption, and tightening quality and environmental regulations. Demand is fundamentally non-discretionary in large-volume applications such as sugar refining and edible oil processing, providing a stable floor. However, organic growth in these mature segments is limited, and value creation is shifting toward specialty grades with selective adsorption profiles, technical service support, and documentation assurance. The market is expected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 4.5% to 5.5% in value terms, with volume growth slightly lower due to premiumization. Process water recycling and zero-liquid-discharge adoption in food manufacturing represent a significant new demand pool, shifting procurement from occasional to continuous operational expenditure. Clean-label trends paradoxically increase reliance on high-performance purification aids to achieve desired sensory and stability outcomes without declared additives. Supply-side risks include feedstock volatility, particularly coconut shell, and rising energy costs for activation and reactivation. Geographically, Asia-Pacific remains the largest and fastest-growing region, driven by food processing expansion and water reuse mandates, while North America and Europe focus on specialty and sustainable reactivation solutions. The market index is projected to reach 155 by 2035 (2025=100), reflecting steady value growth amid structural shifts toward higher-performance grades. Sugar refining remains the largest volume outlet for food grade activated carbon, used extensively for decolorization and removal of off-flavors and impurities from cane and beet sugar streams. Demand is non-discretionary and tied to throughput, providing a stable base. Through 2035, growth will be moderate, aligned with population and processed food consumption, but value growth will outpace volume as refiners adopt higher-performance carbons to meet tighter color specifications and reduce dosage. Demand-side indicators include global sugar production, refinery utilization rates, and adoption of specialty sugar products. The shift toward clean-label and organic sugars may increase purification intensity to avoid alternative chemical treatments. Major trends include process optimization to reduce carbon consumption, increased use of reactivation services, and supplier consolidation. Current trend: Stable volume growth, with premiumization toward higher-purity grades for specialty sugars.. Major trends: Increasing demand for high-purity grades to meet tighter color specifications, Adoption of reactivation services to reduce costs and environmental footprint, Process optimization to minimize carbon dosage, and Growth in specialty and organic sugar segments requiring enhanced purification. Representative participants: Cabot Corporation, Calgon Carbon Corporation (Kuraray), Haycarb PLC, and Jacobi Carbons. Edible oil processing uses activated carbon for removal of color bodies, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and off-flavors, particularly in vegetable oils and fats. Demand is closely linked to global vegetable oil production and consumption, which continues to rise with population and dietary changes. Through 2035, growth will be steady, with increasing emphasis on removal of specific contaminants such as glycidyl esters and 3-MCPD, driven by regulatory limits. Demand-side indicators include vegetable oil production volumes, regulatory changes on contaminant limits, and adoption of premium and specialty oils. The segment is also seeing a shift toward selective adsorption carbons that preserve desirable minor components like tocopherols. Major trends include stricter contaminant regulations, growth in specialty oils, and efficiency improvements. Current trend: Moderate growth driven by vegetable oil consumption and tightening contaminant limits.. artigo.texto: A China Railway Rolling Stock Corporation (CRRC), fabricante de trens, quer montar em Sergipe os grandes sistemas de baterias que guardam energia elétrica para a rede, mas o projeto depende de um ajuste nos incentivos fiscais do estado, que não tem regra pronta para esse tipo de indústria. A proposta prevê investimento acima de US$ 10 milhões, 130 empregos diretos e uma unidade em área de cerca de 15 mil metros quadrados, e a empresa discutiu as condições nesta sexta-feira (13) com o governo do estado. A unidade vai montar os packs de baterias, os conjuntos de células que formam o equipamento, e integrar os contêineres que abrigam os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), sigla em inglês para Battery Energy Storage System. Esses sistemas acumulam a eletricidade gerada por usinas solares e eólicas e a devolvem ao sistema elétrico nos horários de maior necessidade, o que reduz o efeito das variações de sol e vento. >> Siga o canal da Movimento Econômico no WhatsApp O foco inicial é o mercado brasileiro, que deve crescer com os leilões nacionais de armazenamento, de acordo com o country manager da CRRC no Brasil, Igor Abreu. A unidade também poderá atender outros países da América Latina. O município da unidade, o cronograma de obras e a data de início da produção não foram divulgados. As condições do projeto serão estudadas por um grupo de trabalho do governo estadual, e o próximo encontro com a empresa está marcado para segunda-feira (16). Empresa pede adiamento de imposto sobre máquinas e componentes O principal ponto em aberto é tributário. A CRRC perguntou se pode ter o diferimento do Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços (ICMS) sobre bens de capital e componentes usados na fabricação dos equipamentos, mecanismo que adia o pagamento do imposto. O governo informou que o Programa Sergipano de Desenvolvimento Industrial (PSDI) já tem instrumentos de incentivo, mas que eles precisarão ser adaptados a um segmento novo no estado. “Como é uma coisa nova, uma transição de grande tecnologia, precisamos fazer as adequações necessárias. É importante que a Secretaria da Fazenda participe do grupo de trabalho para tirar dúvidas e definir o que pode ser construído”, disse o secretário de Desenvolvimento Econômico e da Ciência e Tecnologia, Valmor Barbosa. O grupo será coordenado pela Casa Civil e terá a Secretaria da Fazenda (Sefaz), a Companhia de Desenvolvimento Econômico de Sergipe (Codise), a Desenvolve-SE e as áreas de infraestrutura, meio ambiente e recursos hídricos. As primeiras reuniões serão presenciais, e as seguintes poderão ser virtuais para acelerar os estudos. O benefício ainda não foi concedido. Também não foram detalhadas as contrapartidas que o estado poderá exigir em empregos, compras de insumos ou contratação de fornecedores locais. Leilões de baterias de dezembro abrem o mercado Os primeiros leilões de reserva de capacidade com baterias do governo federal estão marcados para 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026, com fornecimento a partir de 1º de agosto de 2028. Para a CRRC, esse primeiro leilão é só o começo da expansão das baterias no Brasil, e a empresa espera novas oportunidades em 2027. A empresa cita a localização de Sergipe como vantagem para distribuir os equipamentos. “Temos, em um raio de 500 quilômetros, cerca de 35 milhões de habitantes. É uma construção estratégica do ponto de vista geográfico, porque são consumidores”, disse Abreu. O governador Fábio Mitidieri apresentou o estado como um território que reúne fontes renováveis e a cadeia de petróleo e gás. “Quando falamos de energias renováveis, existe um interesse das empresas em vir para o Nordeste pela posição geográfica, pelas oportunidades e por tudo que estamos construindo. Sergipe se coloca nessa dianteira, porque tem um pouco de todas as matrizes”, afirmou. A empresa disse querer pôr o projeto em prática o mais rápido possível, mas ainda não anunciou a decisão de investir. “Acreditamos no potencial desse investimento e também na oportunidade de gerar empregos e contribuir para o crescimento econômico do estado”, disse o vice-presidente para as Américas da unidade de energia abrangente da CRRC, Zhou Heng, conhecido como Star Zhou. Moura investe R$ 200 milhões em baterias em Pernambuco No mesmo mercado no Nordeste, o Grupo Moura anunciou nesta semana que prevê investir cerca de R$ 200 milhões para fornecer sistemas BESS às empresas que disputarem o leilão de dezembro. Os equipamentos serão montados no complexo da empresa em Belo Jardim, no Agreste pernambucano, com capacidade de fornecimento acima de 8 GWh. A Moura também tem uma parceira chinesa, a CATL, que entra com a tecnologia de armazenamento. A fabricante pernambucana fica com a industrialização e a integração dos sistemas no Brasil, arranjo montado para cumprir as exigências de conteúdo local previstas para o leilão. A empresa apresentou em 2019 o Moura BESS, sistema que produz em Belo Jardim, e soma mais de 40 projetos instalados no país, em indústria, agronegócio, saúde, saneamento e no setor elétrico. O valor anunciado inclui uma expansão recente da fábrica e um novo ciclo de ampliação e modernização. CRRC já fabrica trens em São Paulo Em Sergipe, o governador também citou o Veículo Leve sobre Trilhos (VLT) da Grande Aracaju como oportunidade para a empresa. “Temos por exemplo, a implantação do VLT da Grande Aracaju, um investimento superior a R$ 700 milhões, que abre oportunidades relacionadas ao setor ferroviário e à cadeia de fornecedores”, disse Mitidieri. artigo.texto: QuantumScape has unveiled Osprey, a next-generation all-solid-state battery platform that could help overcome some of the biggest obstacles facing solid-state battery development. The company’s latest technology has demonstrated 1,000 charge cycles, five-minute fast charging and operation under just one atmosphere of pressure, potentially bringing solid-state batteries closer to practical automotive applications. The announcement marks an important development for QuantumScape as it expands its solid-state battery technology beyond its existing QSE platform. Osprey is designed as an open platform that supports different cathode chemistries and creates new opportunities for licensing and joint development with automotive manufacturers and battery developers. QuantumScape’s Osprey Platform Targets Major Solid-State Battery Challenges Osprey combines QuantumScape’s proprietary ceramic separator and anode-free lithium-metal design with a solid cathode to create an all-solid-state battery cell. One of the most significant aspects of the announcement is the company’s demonstration of a sulfide-based solid-state battery cathode capable of completing 1,000 charge cycles under just one atmosphere of pressure. This is particularly important because sulfide-based solid-state batteries have faced two major technical challenges: chemical reactions between sulfide electrolytes and lithium metal, which can shorten battery life, and the need for high operating pressure to maintain performance. Both limitations have made it difficult to develop sulfide-based solid-state batteries suitable for mass-market electric vehicles. QuantumScape says Osprey addresses these challenges while delivering performance characteristics that could make the technology more practical for automotive applications. 1,000 Charge Cycles and Five-Minute Fast Charging Early testing has produced several promising results, particularly in battery longevity, charging speed and operating conditions. According to QuantumScape, Osprey cells have demonstrated the following performance: – Cycle life: 1,000 full charge cycles with approximately 80% capacity retention under gold-standard testing conditions. – Fast charging: Charging from 10% to 80% in approximately five minutes. – Operating pressure: Just one atmosphere of pressure, significantly reducing the pressure requirements associated with conventional sulfide-based solid-state battery designs. – Cold-weather performance: Operation at temperatures below -20°C (-4°F). – Energy density: Projected volumetric energy density of up to approximately 1,100 Wh/L. The five-minute charging capability is particularly noteworthy. If achieved in production-ready automotive battery packs, it could significantly reduce charging times and make electric vehicles more convenient for long-distance travel. The low-pressure requirement is another important development. Reducing the need for heavy pressure-management systems could simplify battery pack engineering and potentially make solid-state battery integration more practical. However, these figures come from early testing and should not be interpreted as confirmed specifications for production electric vehicles. Real-world performance will depend on further development, validation and battery pack integration. Higher Energy Density and Improved Cold-Weather Performance Beyond charging speed and durability, Osprey is designed to deliver additional performance benefits through its combination of solid cathode technology and QuantumScape’s proprietary ceramic separator. The company projects energy densities of up to approximately 1,100 Wh/L. Higher volumetric energy density could allow automakers to develop batteries that store more energy within the same physical space. For electric vehicles, this could translate into longer driving ranges without necessarily increasing battery pack size. Alternatively, manufacturers could use smaller and lighter battery packs while maintaining competitive driving ranges. Cold-weather performance is another important consideration. Conventional electric vehicle batteries can experience reduced efficiency and charging performance in low temperatures. QuantumScape says Osprey cells have demonstrated operation below -20°C, potentially offering greater flexibility for vehicles operating in colder climates. The technology has also demonstrated an enhanced safety profile compared with conventional lithium-ion cells, according to QuantumScape. An Open Platform for Different Battery Chemistries Unlike a battery design limited to a single cathode chemistry, Osprey is intended to support multiple solid cathode approaches. QuantumScape has already tested the platform using solid cathodes developed both internally and by its automotive customers. This approach could provide manufacturers and battery developers with greater flexibility when developing their own solid-state battery technologies. The company is also expanding its commercial strategy. Osprey builds on the existing QSE platform while creating additional licensing and co-development opportunities for current customers and companies working on sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries. This open-platform approach could help QuantumScape expand its reach across the automotive industry without relying exclusively on developing and supplying complete battery cells itself. QuantumScape Wants to Make Osprey a Leading Solid-State Battery Platform Dr. Siva Sivaram, president and CEO of QuantumScape, described Osprey as the result of years of advanced research and development. He said the battery industry has invested heavily in sulfide-based solid-state technology but has repeatedly encountered fundamental technical limitations. QuantumScape believes its latest platform can address these problems and unlock more of the potential of all-solid-state batteries. artigo.texto: In a letter to the county, developers of the Project Pegasus data center requested the public hearing for the data center's property to be scheduled in the new year. The rezoning hearing was tentatively scheduled for Dec. 1, however, the developers requested a new date so they can hold a second community meeting. The Project Pegasus community meeting, which is mandated by the county's data center ordinance, was held on Oct. 22 and the developers placed signs near the property, advertised in The Newnan Times-Herald and sent mailers to nearby property owners to alert residents about the meeting. According to the letter, on the day of the community meeting, someone removed the signs posted on the potential data center's property without the developers' permission. The county's ordinance requires the notice for the community meeting to remain on the property until the meeting is over. "Consequently, due to no fault of the Applicant, the signs did not remind posted for the required time," stated the letter. To meet the ordinance's requirements, the developers are planning a second community meeting, according to the letter. "It is not possible for the Applicant to give notice of and host another community meeting before the (Board of Commissioners) Dec. 1, 2026, public hearing," states the letter. In the letter, the developers said they plan to hold a second community meeting during the first or second week of December. Briana Gregory, communications specialist for the county, said the public hearing for Project Pegasus is now tentatively scheduled for Jan. 21, 2027.

artigo.texto: EGI Battery Opens Japan Technical Center to Advance Development and Commercialization of Next-Generation Battery Cells Yokohama-based EGI Battery KK launches its Japan Technical Center to strengthen R&D, materials science, and supply-chain capabilities to support advanced lithium-ion battery development, manufacturing, supplier partnerships and customer relationships across Asia Pacific. ANN ARBOR, Mich., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — EGI Battery, a U.S.-owned lithium-ion battery cell company, today announces the establishment of EGI Battery KK, its Japanese subsidiary, and the official opening of its Japan Technical Center in Yokohama. Japan’s history of battery innovation, advanced manufacturing know-how and experienced talent make it a strategic location to bolster EGI’s technical operations. EGI Battery KK’s Technical Center will initially focus on conducting research & development, evaluating advanced battery materials, and strengthening supplier relationships and technology partnerships to support EGI’s advanced battery cell development and commercialization efforts. Tom McGuckin, CEO of EGI Battery, said: Building better batteries takes more than a breakthrough in the lab. ”It takes capabilities to connect materials, engineering and manufacturing to produce batteries which enable our customers’ technology. Establishing EGI Battery KK is a strategic investment in those capabilities. By connecting Japan’s deep battery expertise with the manufacturing operations we are building in Michigan, we aim to bring the next generation of advanced lithium-ion batteries into production and expand what our customers can achieve.” EGI Battery KK also establishes a local base for working directly with customers and partners across Asia Pacific. The team will help connect regional market needs with EGI’s cell development and commercialization efforts. McGuckin added, “This regional presence deepens collaboration between our technical development activities and our customers’ applications.” Junji Tabuchi, President of EGI Battery KK, will lead the Yokohama operation, including its technical partnerships and regional business development activities. Tabuchi brings more than 35 years of lithium-ion battery experience across UBE Corporation, NEC TOKIN and E-One Moli Energy, including leadership of battery materials R&D at UBE. Tabuchi, said: The opportunity is not only to develop better battery materials, but to turn those advances into cells that can be manufactured reliably and meet demanding customer requirements “Our initial focus is on materials, R&D and our supplier partnerships. We are intentionally building a strong technical foundation in Japan so we can move promising research and engineering into commercial production.” As the Japan operations develop, EGI Battery KK plans to expand into cell design, with a focus on electrodes, and then battery manufacturing capabilities. These future capabilities will leverage the center’s initial materials, supply-chain and R&D activities, strengthening EGI’s ability to develop and validate new battery technologies. The Japan Technical Center complements EGI’s manufacturing expansion in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Through a phased approach, EGI is building the production capabilities and technical expertise needed to manufacture advanced lithium-ion pouch cells at scale. The Japan operation’s initial materials evaluation, R&D and supplier collaboration will support that work, strengthening the connection between battery innovation and U.S. production. artigo.texto: Baterista do Duran Duran, Roger Taylor deixa a banda por agravamento de zumbido no ouvido Aos 66 anos, baterista decidiu priorizar a saúde e seguir recomendações médicas; músico integrava a formação original da banda desde 1978 Por O Globo Atualizado O baterista Roger Taylor anunciou que deixará o Duran Duran após o agravamento gradual de um zumbido no ouvido. Aos 66 anos, o músico afirmou que decidiu priorizar a saúde e seguir as recomendações de seus médicos. Integrante da formação original da banda, ele entrou para o grupo em 1978, saiu em 1985 e retornou em 2001. Taylor descreveu sua trajetória no Duran Duran como "a alegria da vida", mas afirmou que a piora da condição tornou necessário considerar os possíveis impactos sobre sua audição. "Tocar bateria nesta banda foi a alegria da minha vida, e nunca conseguirei agradecer devidamente aos fãs pelo carinho que demonstraram por nós ao longo dos anos Mas a verdade é que meu zumbido no ouvido vem piorando gradualmente", afirmou. O músico disse que teve dificuldade para decidir o momento de sua saída, mas ficou satisfeito por encerrar sua trajetória no grupo após uma sequência de apresentações e projetos que considerou especialmente marcantes. Apoio da banda Os integrantes Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes e John Taylor afirmaram que a decisão foi tomada após "cuidadosa consideração e orientação médica", que indicaram que "proteger sua audição e sua saúde a longo prazo deve ser agora a prioridade". Em mensagem conjunta, os músicos destacaram a importância de Roger Taylor para a história e a sonoridade do Duran Duran. "Roger é nosso irmão", disseram. "Sua bateria ajudou a definir o som do Duran Duran desde o início, e tê-lo de volta conosco desde 2001 foi extremamente importante para todos nós. Apoiamos totalmente sua decisão e desejamos a ele saúde e felicidade. Ele sempre fará parte desta família, enquanto continuamos explorando projetos novos e empolgantes com a banda". Últimos trabalhos Taylor afirmou que encerra sua participação depois de um período marcado por apresentações importantes e novos trabalhos. Entre os momentos recentes citados estão uma turnê pelo Reino Unido e pela Europa, a segunda apresentação do Duran Duran como atração principal no festival BST Hyde Park, a entrada no Rock & Roll Hall of Fame e o retorno ao estúdio com Nile Rodgers. "Acabamos de voltar de uma turnê extremamente bem-sucedida pelo Reino Unido e pela Europa, que veio após nossa segunda apresentação como atração principal no BST Hyde Park, nossa entrada no Rock & Roll Hall of Fame e nosso retorno ao estúdio com Nile Rodgers. Não poderia ter pedido um capítulo final melhor, com tantos momentos especiais que guardarei para sempre. Sigo em frente com enorme orgulho e apenas amor por Simon, Nick e John", afirmou. Ao longo de sua trajetória, o baterista participou de dez álbuns de sucesso e de músicas que alcançaram destaque nas paradas, incluindo os singles "Is There Something I Should Know?" e "The Reflex", ambos chegaram ao primeiro lugar, além de "A View to a Kill", tema do filme de James Bond lançado em 1985. Homenagem do filho O filho de Roger Taylor também publicou uma homenagem ao pai no Instagram, acompanhada de fotografias da banda. Na mensagem, destacou os registros que fez dos bastidores ao longo dos anos e manifestou orgulho da carreira do músico. "Por trás das câmeras, tive a sorte de registrar momentos incríveis ao longo dos anos. Mas nada se compara a ver seu pai fazendo aquilo que ama. Ao pendurar as baquetas, que carreira, que legado! Tenho muito orgulho de você, pai. Que venha o próximo capítulo da vida!"

artigo.texto: Incentivo a data centers no Brasil contrasta com rejeição nos EUA Enquanto o país reduz imposto e governos locais disputam investimentos, oposição de americanos a essas estruturas afetou eleição por lá Enquanto o governo do presidente Lula se esforça para atrair projetos de data centers para o Brasil, a expansão dessa infraestrutura enfrenta resistência crescente nos Estados Unidos, chegando a influenciar o recente resultado das eleições estaduais e parlamentares no país, desfavorável à gestão de Donald Trump. - O preço da ‘ressaca digital’: quanto custou ao mundo a pane global do Outlook da Microsoft? - Nvidia: entenda por que escândalo que derrubou CEO acirra disputa entre EUA e China por chips de IA A insatisfação de americanos com o consumo de água desses empreendimentos e o impacto que o seu consumo de energia tem em suas contas de luz foi apontado com um dos fatores para a derrota de republicanos em estados como Virgínia e Texas. A disparada da demanda de energia dos data centers e a sobrecarga das redes elétricas estão estimulando uma nova onda de geração de eletricidade a gás natural e pressionando os compromissos climáticos das grandes empresas de tecnologia. Esse ponto é o principal diferencial entre os dois países na questão. O Brasil busca consumidores para seu alto potencial de geração de energia elétrica de fontes renováveis. O país enfrenta cortes na geração de energia eólica e solar excedente para preservar a segurança do sistema elétrico e dispõe de uma ampla carteira de projetos de energia verde em paralelo aos planos de novos data centers. - Escândalo da Nvidia: 'Culto ao fundador' moldou o Vale do Silício e põe em xeque futuro da empresa Enquanto políticos americanos enfrentam protestos, o Congresso brasileiro aprovou uma legislação que reduz drasticamente os impostos sobre equipamentos de tecnologia da informação e governos estaduais e municipais disputam megaprojetos como o Rio AI City, na capital fluminense, de R$ 360 bilhões em dez anos, ou o data center da ByteDance, dona do TikTok, em construção na área do porto de Pecém, no Ceará, que deve alcançar R$ 200 bilhões. Corrida regional Estão de olho no Brasil grandes operadoras de infraestrutura de computação em nuvem, conhecidas como hyperscalers, dos EUA e da China, para projetos que custarão dezenas de bilhões de dólares. Diferentemente dos EUA, que está no centro do desenvolvimento tecnólogico global há décadas, o que está em jogo no Brasil é a ambição do país de se tornar o principal polo de capacidade computacional para inteligência artificial (IA) da América Latina, à frente de concorrentes como Argentina e Chile, que oferecem incentivos e constroem infraestrutura para disputar os mesmos investimentos, inclusive na área complementar de energia. O Brasil já está atrás do Chile na implantação de baterias de armazenamento de energia em grande escala, por exemplo. Os data centers também enfrentaram protestos no Brasil, especialmente de grupos indígenas preocupados com o grande consumo de água dessas estruturas para refrigeração de máquinas, mas a oposição não ganhou a mesma dimensão observada nos EUA, onde cerca de 70% dos entrevistados disseram ser contrários à construção dessas instalações em suas comunidades, segundo uma pesquisa do Gallup realizada em março.

artigo.texto: Press release — Nidec Showcases Advanced Energy Storage and Power Conversion Technologies at RE+ 2026 - Nidec introduces ACBOX™ V4, DCBOX™ and UniQube™, designed to address evolving grid requirements, support renewable integration and improve system performance. - Grid-forming capabilities, scalable power conversion and integrated system architectures help customers strengthen grid reliability and simplify project deployment. - Nidec combines advanced technologies, engineering expertise and long-term service capabilities to support customers across the energy infrastructure lifecycle. Las Vegas, NV – November 12, 2026 – As electricity demand grows and energy infrastructure becomes increasingly complex, Nidec Conversion, a business of Nidec and a global provider of power conversion and energy storage solutions, will showcase its latest technologies at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas. Featuring the ACBOX™ V4 integrated battery energy storage system (BESS) and UniQube™ high-power conversion platform, combined with DCBOX™ or as a standalone equipment, Nidec will demonstrate how advanced engineering and integrated technologies are helping customers address evolving grid requirements, improve system performance and support the deployment of energy storage at scale. "Energy infrastructure is entering a new phase, where reliability, flexibility and the ability to integrate increasingly complex technologies are becoming essential," said Michael Briggs, Chairman, Nidec Motion & Energy Business Unit, CEO, Appliance Automotive Division. "At Nidec, we are bringing together our engineering expertise, advanced technologies and global scale to help customers address these challenges. Our focus is on strengthening the technologies and capabilities that will support the world's growing energy needs." "Customers need solutions that not only meet today's technical requirements but also adapt as their projects and the grid evolve," said Dominique Llonch, President, Nidec Motion & Energy Business Unit. "ACBOX™ V4, DCBOX™ and UniQube™ reflect our commitment to practical innovation, combining advanced technologies with engineering expertise to help customers simplify integration, improve performance and support long-term operations. Together, these solutions demonstrate how Nidec is responding to evolving energy infrastructure needs, from renewable integration and grid stability to the growing power demands of data centers." UniQube™: High-Power Conversion for Evolving Energy Storage Requirements UniQube™ is Nidec's new liquid-cooled power conversion system (PCS) platform, engineered to support large-scale energy storage applications, including systems with storage durations of two to eight hours. Its modular architecture provides flexible configurations to accommodate different project requirements. Designed for outdoor installation, UniQube™ uses liquid cooling to support consistent performance in demanding environments, including high-temperature climates. Its compact architecture delivers up to 20% higher power density compared with the stated market benchmark, helping customers optimize available space and simplify system integration. The platform supports current 1500 V applications and is designed to accommodate the industry's transition toward 2000 V systems. Its flexible architecture also supports applications beyond battery storage, including solar and hydrogen-related energy infrastructure. ACBOX™ V4: Integrated Energy Storage with Advanced Grid-Forming Capabilities ACBOX™ V4represents the latest evolution of Nidec's integrated AC-block BESS architecture, designed to address increasingly demanding grid requirements while supporting system efficiency, reliability and scalability. Engineered with a distributed power conversion architecture incorporating silicon-carbide (SiC) semiconductor technology, ACBOX™ V4 enables more granular energy management and is designed to improve system efficiency and availability. Native grid-forming capabilities help support grid stability and resilience, enabling energy storage systems to play a more active role in modern power networks as renewable generation increases. The platform also incorporates a cybersecurity-by-design approach and supply chain transparency considerations to address growing customer expectations around system security, equipment sourcing and long-term operational confidence. Integrated Capabilities for the Evolving Energy Market Nidec combines proprietary hardware and software developed in-house with manufacturing, system integration and project execution capabilities. Through regional engineering expertise, local project execution and long-term lifecycle services, Nidec offers customers an integrated partner across the energy storage project lifecycle, helping simplify execution, manage complexity and support reliable system performance. As energy infrastructure needs evolve, Nidec continues to connect its technologies and expertise across the business to deliver practical innovations that create long-term value for customers. Visit Nidec at RE+ 2026 Nidec will showcase ACBOX™ V4, DCBOX™ and UniQube™, and its broader energy storage and power conversion capabilities at booth C5454 in Central Hall at the Las Vegas Convention Center, November 17–19, 2026. For media inquiries, please contact: Marco Lastrico - m.lastrico@barabinousa.com Filippo Berlè - f.berle@barabinousa.com Anna Szczesniak - anna.szczesniak@nidec-motor.com About Nidec Nidec is the world’s leading manufacturer of electric motors, drives, and controls, powering nearly everything that spins and moves, from smartphones and household appliances to electric vehicles, factories, data centers, aircraft, and critical infrastructure. Founded in 1973 and headquartered in Kyoto, Japan, Nidec operates more than 300 group companies across 40+ countries, with over 100,000 employees worldwide. artigo.texto: This new semi-solid-state power bank has a 20,000mAh capacity, 100W of power, and is safer than most alternatives 20,000mAh of relatively safe battery power - The BMX SolidSafe 20K uses semi-solid-state battery tech for safer, longer-lasting power - It has a 20,000mAh capacity and 100W of power - It's priced at $109.99 (roughly £85 / AU$160) Semi-solid-state batteries are the big new thing in power banks, delivering increased capacities without a bigger footprint. They're also slower to degrade — so they won’t need replacing as fast — and are even deemed to be safer than conventional lithium-ion power banks, as most of the liquid found in those devices is replaced with a solid or gel electrolyte, which is less flammable. That last point is one of the big features BMX is pushing about its new 20,000mAh SolidSafe power bank, an accessory notable for being semi-solid-state and having a higher capacity than most battery packs of its kind. While many rival products with this battery tech are most suited to charging phones and tablets, the SolidSafe 20K can comfortably charge a laptop, with BMX claiming — via Gadgeteer — that it’s good for one full charge of a 13.6-inch MacBook Air M3 with power left over. Three ports so you can charge everything Of course, it can charge phones and tablets too, and it has up to 100W of charging power. You’ll get that much power if you just plug one thing in via its primary USB-C port, but it also has a secondary USB-C port, which individually can manage 65W, and a USB-A port, capable of 22.5W. Use all three ports at once, and you’ll get 65W from the primary one and 7.5W from the other two. The SolidSafe 20K also has a tiny color LCD screen that shows the battery percentage and wattage on each port, and it comes in at 147.4 x 90.3 x 18mm and 375g, making it a lot slimmer than many laptop power banks — so it’s ideal for travel, especially as it falls under the 100W carry-on limit for spare batteries on most airlines. The work has begun after the company had secured about $850 million in construction and term financing commitments for the project. Energizar is the second large BESS of Flatiron in Massachusetts, after the 200 MW/800 MWh Taft Project in Uxbridge. artigo.texto: The Philippines has joined Vietnam and Indonesia in a new regional partnership aimed at accelerating the clean energy transition in remote and island communities. The initiative, launched on November 10 at the COP31 Philippine Hub in Antalya, Türkiye, will focus on replacing expensive diesel-powered generators with solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage solutions. The partnership aims to improve electricity access, reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels and lower power generation costs in isolated communities. It will also encourage regional cooperation to develop renewable energy projects that can provide reliable and affordable electricity to underserved populations. During the launch event, Department of Energy Undersecretary Felix William Fuentebella announced that the Philippine government is planning to integrate island electrification into its Green Energy Auction program. The proposed approach would allow renewable energy developers to participate in auctions designed to support clean power generation in off-grid areas. However, specific auction rounds, implementation timelines and capacity allocations have not yet been finalized. The need for this transition is highlighted by the country’s existing dependence on oil-based power generation. According to official data, as of December 2025, approximately 94% of the Philippines’ off-grid power plants, representing 421 out of 447 facilities, continued to rely heavily on oil. This dependence results in high electricity generation costs and limits the availability of reliable power in several remote communities. Successful pilot projects demonstrate the potential benefits of solar and battery storage systems. On Cobrador Island in Romblon, a 30-kilowatt solar-plus-battery hybrid installation reduced electricity generation costs by nearly 50%, from $0.47 to $0.24 per kilowatt-hour. The project also increased electricity availability from just eight hours daily to continuous 24-hour service. Regional research, including studies by Indonesia’s Institute for Essential Services Reform, suggests that combining solar power with battery storage can deliver electricity at approximately one-third of the cost of conventional diesel generation. Beyond individual projects, the partnership between the Philippines, Vietnam and Indonesia will promote coordinated planning, private investment, supportive regulations and technical capacity development. The initiative aims to transform successful island electrification pilots into scalable renewable energy projects. Through regional collaboration and greater deployment of solar and battery storage, the participating countries seek to improve energy affordability, strengthen electricity reliability and support long-term climate resilience in remote communities. Project “Ragow”, located in Brandenburg, near Berlin, ranks among the largest in Europe. Acquired by Flower in 2025, the project has now reached a new milestone with the submission of building permit applications. It is expected to reach ready-to-build status in 2027, with commercial operation targeted for 2029. Under the agreement, dces will oversee project development with support from Flower, while Flower will be responsible for financing, EPC, operation and commercialization of the asset. “This marks a key milestone for Flower and an important leap forward for both the German and the wider European energy system. As renewables continue to expand, the need for large-scale battery storage systems that can mitigate volatility, improve grid efficiency and accelerate renewable energy build-out is increasing rapidly. With support from dces, we are now taking another vital step toward a cleaner, more affordable and more secure energy system,” said John Diklev, founder and CEO of Flower. dces group – a leading project developer in Germany dces group is one of Germany’s most established developers of large-scale BESS assets, with 12 years of market presence and a 3 GW project pipeline across Germany. The company focuses on planning, development and stakeholder management across several of the country’s largest storage projects. “The partnership with Flower aligns with our mission to accelerate the scaling of large-scale BESS in Germany. With Flower’s end-to-end battery storage expertise, and our track record in project development, we are committed to developing an essential piece of infrastructure that will drive the energy transition in Germany and beyond,” said Jens Schmidthammer, founder and Partner at dces group. Flower’s expansion in Germany and Europe Flower has scaled significantly in Germany since entering the market in 2025. During 2026 alone, the energy tech company acquired a 112 MW BESS project portfolio from Chint Solar, acquired a 63 / 257 MWh BESS project in Saxony-Anhalt, started construction of an internally developed BESS projects in Hamburg (100 MW / 400 MWh), and reached ready-to-build for an internally developed 10 MW / 20 MWh project in Saarland. Furthermore, the company has signed a virtual Flexibility Purchase Agreement (“FPA”, also referred to as a virtual toll) in Germany with global energy group ENGIE, securing financing for a combined capacity of 126 MW of BESS. In 2027, the company plans to roll out its proprietary asset optimization algorithms in the German market, enabling advanced orchestration of energy assets to drive stability, profitability and efficiency in the German energy system. Alongside its rapid expansion in Germany, Flower is advancing several large-scale projects in the Netherlands, France, and Belgium, growing its multi-GWh development pipeline across Europe. artigo.texto: Texas Democrat's data center opposition may cloud power plant's commercial viability: lawmaker Summary Rep. Hong Kee-won said the Democratic Party’s takeover of both chambers of the U.S. Congress will complicate pending Seoul-Washington negotiations, as agreements on submarines, uranium enrichment and U.S. investment require congressional approval and legislation. Speaking in an interview on Wednesday, he said the Texas power plant and Alaska LNG projects face greater commercial uncertainty after cautious positions from Democratic governors-elect. Hong urged Seoul to engage more with Democratic lawmakers and explain its positions. He also said the alliance remains firm and that transferring wartime operational control can proceed without weakening allied readiness. Key Facts - Hong is a two-term lawmaker with the ruling Democratic Party of Korea and was named vice chairman of the National Assembly’s Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee on Aug. 11. - The Texas gas-fired power plant was selected as the first project under Korea’s $350 billion investment commitment and is intended to supply electricity to data centers. - Seoul has made no commitment to the Alaska LNG project and is still reviewing its commercial viability. - Hong said Korean lawmakers should use the Korea-U.S. Parliamentarians’ Union, launched last year, to engage with their American counterparts. - Hong said Coupang generates most of its revenue in Korea, although it is legally incorporated in the United States. Democratic victory in Congress would complicate Seoul-Washington negotiations, says Rep. Hong Kee-won The Democratic Party’s takeover of both chambers of the U.S. Congress will complicate pending negotiations between Seoul and Washington and Korea must step up efforts to explain its positions to U.S. lawmakers, said Rep. Hong Kee-won, vice chairman of the National Assembly’s Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee. Even though the two governments had already reached agreements on nuclear-powered submarines, uranium enrichment programs and investment in the U.S., Hong said the “situation has become more complex than when Republicans held the majority,” as advancing those initiatives requires congressional approval and legislation. “Previously, securing an agreement with the administration alone was enough, whereas now we must build a degree of consensus within Congress to move forward,” Hong said in an interview with The Korea Times on Wednesday. Hong, a two-term lawmaker with the ruling Democratic Party of Korea, previously served as a diplomat and presidential adviser specializing in China and trade. He was named vice chairman of the National Assembly committee on Aug. 11. His remarks came amid lingering friction in Seoul-Washington security and trade ties, ranging from delays in investment negotiations to restrictions on intelligence sharing about North Korea, with many expecting that the Democrats’ recent electoral victory may not necessarily benefit South Korea. Hong said uncertainty has grown on two fronts after Democratic governors-elect in Texas and Alaska took cautious positions. The first is a gas-fired power plant in Texas, selected as the first project under Korea’s $350 billion investment commitment under the joint fact sheet between the two countries. The plant is intended to supply electricity to data centers in the state. The second is the Alaska liquefied natural gas (LNG) pipeline project, which U.S. President Donald Trump has pressed Seoul to join. Unlike the Texas plant, the Alaska project has not been confirmed as part of the investment package; Seoul has made no commitment and is still reviewing its commercial viability. For Seoul, the electoral shift raises fresh doubts about commercial viability, which remains a point of contention between the two countries. “While the U.S. government needs to guarantee that offtake demand, the Texas power plant deal was made without such assurances. Now, with a Democratic governor-elect in Texas taking a cautious stance on data center expansion, uncertainty has grown over whether even the first project can be commercially viable and attract buyers for its electricity once the plant is built,” he said. On the Alaska project, he noted, “Given that Democrats oppose the Alaska LNG project over environmental concerns, uncertainty surrounding these initiatives has undeniably grown and the situation may change.” Despite the differences, Hong said the alliance between Seoul and Washington remains “firm,” describing recent U.S. visa reviews and denials involving Korean lawmakers as individual cases resulting from stricter screening rather than a broader political signal. He called on Seoul to intensify its engagement with Washington to clear up misunderstandings and move negotiations forward. “Korea must step up outreach to Democratic lawmakers in the U.S. to build consensus. In particular, Seoul needs to reassure Congress that its nuclear-powered submarine and civilian uranium enrichment programs pose no proliferation risks,” he said, adding that Korean lawmakers should actively engage with their American counterparts through the Korea-U.S. Parliamentarians' Union, a group launched last year. artigo.texto: BELOIT — The Beloit City Council on Monday night is going to discuss whether the city should adopt a 12-month moratorium against possible data center developments to give it time to review its zoning and land use codes. Earlier this year, both the Towns of Turtle and Beloit adopted moratoriums after public outrage when a California-based company proposed building a $1 billion hyperscale data center on property that would spill over into both towns. To date, there has been no interest, at least that’s been released publicly, in building a hyperscale data center within the City of Beloit. Dozens of communities have turned to moratoriums to halt or slow data center development in their communities as public opinion has largely moved against the high tech industry over concerns of excessive power and water use. According to a moratorium tracker by the webiste interconnectedcapital.com — www.interconnectedcapital.com/research/data-center-moratoriums — there are now 395 active data center moratoriums in the United States and 57 different communities have adopted outright bans on data centers.

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no Por que empresas de inteligência artificial estão investindo bilhões em data centers? Publicado 15/11/2026 • 10:00 | Atualizado há 23 horas Secretário de Tesouro dos EUA pede “reestruturação drástica” na Nvidia e contratação de novo CEO ‘Dormimos aqui’: atrasos em voos persistem enquanto companhias aéreas se esforçam para se recuperar da paralisação das operações Espiã da Nvidia: Megaspeed afirma que Alice Huang deixou a empresa em 2025 e abre investigação interna sobre reportagens relacionadas aos seus negócios SpaceX captura o estágio superior do foguete Starship em um feito histórico Como o lançamento de GTA VI pode transformar os setores de games e streaming e até influenciar pedidos de folga no trabalho KEY POINTS Foto: pexels A expansão da inteligência artificial (IA) está aumentando a demanda por infraestrutura capaz de processar grandes volumes de informações. Por trás de ferramentas como chatbots, assistentes virtuais e sistemas de geração de imagens, existe uma estrutura de data centers que exige investimentos elevados em servidores, chips, energia e refrigeração. Por isso, empresas de tecnologia estão ampliando seus compromissos com projetos de computação de alto desempenho. Um exemplo envolve a Anthropic, criadora do Claude, a empresa TeraWulf e o Google, que entrou como garantidor financeiro de um empreendimento com aproximadamente US$ 19 bilhões (cerca de R$ 106,09 bilhões) em compromissos de aluguel. Leia também: Economia do Reino Unido cresce 0,7% no terceiro trimestre, impulsionada pela inteligência artificial O projeto prevê a construção de um complexo de data centers em Hawesville, no estado de Kentucky, nos Estados Unidos. Além disso, a estrutura terá capacidade estimada de 401 megawatts e atenderá às necessidades de processamento da Anthropic para desenvolver e operar seus sistemas de inteligência artificial. O desenvolvimento de modelos de IA exige grande capacidade computacional. Durante o treinamento, esses sistemas processam enormes volumes de dados e realizam cálculos complexos. Depois, precisam manter essa capacidade para responder aos comandos dos usuários e executar diferentes tarefas. Dessa forma, para sustentar essas operações, as empresas precisam de servidores especializados, chips de alto desempenho e fornecimento constante de energia. Além disso, os equipamentos geram calor durante o processamento, o que exige sistemas de refrigeração para manter o funcionamento adequado. Dessa forma, construir um data center envolve custos que vão além da instalação de computadores: também é necessário investir em terrenos, infraestrutura elétrica e equipamentos especializados. O empreendimento em Kentucky está ligado a um contrato de 20 anos entre a Anthropic e a TeraWulf. Os compromissos de aluguel previstos no acordo somam aproximadamente US$ 19 bilhões. A construção ocorrerá em etapas. A previsão é que os primeiros espaços comecem a ser disponibilizados no fim de 2027, com as entregas avançando até o segundo trimestre de 2028. Além disso, a TeraWulf também ampliou seu acordo com a Fluor Enterprises, responsável pelos serviços de engenharia, aquisição de equipamentos e construção de três edifícios do complexo. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC A participação do Google busca reduzir os riscos financeiros do projeto. A companhia oferecerá garantias para determinadas obrigações da Anthropic relacionadas ao pagamento do aluguel dos data centers. Na prática, esse mecanismo dá mais segurança à TeraWulf para buscar empréstimos de longo prazo e captar recursos para a construção. O acordo também prevê alternativas caso a Anthropic deixe de pagar o aluguel ou enfrente um processo de insolvência. Nessas situações, o Google poderá assumir o contrato como inquilino e realizar os pagamentos. Outra possibilidade, sob determinadas condições, é quitar uma taxa de rescisão e receber uma participação societária na Raylan Data, subsidiária da TeraWulf responsável pelo projeto. Portanto, o Google não está investindo diretamente os US$ 19 bilhões na construção. O valor corresponde aos compromissos estimados de aluguel da Anthropic ao longo de 20 anos. A garantia oferecida pela companhia ajuda a melhorar as condições de financiamento do empreendimento. O projeto também acompanha uma mudança no mercado de infraestrutura digital. A TeraWulf, que tem origem na mineração de Bitcoin, vem direcionando seus negócios para instalações de computação de alto desempenho, aproveitando a demanda crescente de empresas de inteligência artificial. Leia também: Inteligência artificial nas escolas: veja o que muda com as novas regras do MEC Esse movimento mostra que a expansão da IA depende não apenas de novos modelos e softwares, mas também de estruturas físicas capazes de sustentar operações em grande escala. Nesse cenário, parcerias entre desenvolvedoras de inteligência artificial, empresas de infraestrutura e grandes companhias de tecnologia ajudam a viabilizar projetos bilionários. Ao oferecer garantias financeiras, o Google contribui para ampliar a capacidade de processamento disponível para o setor e reforça a importância dos data centers na corrida pela inteligência artificial. 🔷 Canal 562 ClaroTV+ | Canal 562 Sky | Canal 592 Vivo | Canal 187 Oi | Operadoras regionais 🔷 TV SINAL ABERTO: parabólicas canal 562 🔷 ONLINE: www.timesbrasil.com.br | YouTube 🔷 FAST Channels: Samsung TV Plus, LG Channels, TCL Channels, Pluto TV, Roku, Zapping | Novos Streamings
