artigo.texto: PangeAI Partners with Sky Blue Impact to Accelerate Data Center Site Analysis with Agentic Geospatial AI Sky Blue Impact uses PangeAI’s plain-English geospatial platform to assess grid, climate and hazard factors across potential data center locations, without lengthy consultant-led studies. PangeAI, the agentic geospatial AI platform, announced that Sky Blue Impact has become a client, using PangeAI to support site analysis for data center development. The work focuses on helping Sky Blue’s team evaluate and compare potential locations earlier and with greater confidence. Agentic geospatial AI screens data center sites for grid access, water and climate risk in minutes, not weeks. As demand for data centers continues to grow, choosing the right location has become one of the most consequential decisions developers make. Beyond land and cost, every candidate site must be evaluated for: - Grid capacity and proximity to existing infrastructure - Water availability for cooling - Climate and hazard exposure, including flooding, wildfire and extreme heat - Permitting and land-use constraints Also Read: AiThority Interview with Gou Rao, co-founder and CEO at NeuBird AI Getting any one of these wrong can delay a project by years or add significant cost over the life of the facility. This analysis has traditionally meant lengthy studies from external GIS and engineering consultants, slowing down early-stage decisions and limiting how many options a team can realistically consider. With PangeAI, Sky Blue Impact’s team can ask site questions in plain English and receive decision-ready answers drawn from Earth-observation, climate and infrastructure data. PangeAI’s autonomous geospatial analyst does the work a GIS specialist would normally do, gathering the relevant data, running the analysis and presenting the results in a form the team can act on. Questions that would typically take a consultant days or weeks to answer can be answered in minutes. Because every site is assessed against the same criteria, the team gets a consistent view of risk and opportunity across all the locations it is considering. Answers come back with the underlying data and maps, so findings can be checked and shared with partners, investors or planning authorities. “Data center siting is a high-stakes decision, and the teams making it shouldn’t have to wait weeks for answers,” said Johanna von der Leyen, CEO and co-founder of PangeAI. “We built PangeAI so that anyone on a development team can ask a question about a site and get a clear, evidence-based answer. Working with Sky Blue Impact shows how quickly that can change the way location decisions get made.” The collaboration reflects PangeAI’s growing focus on data centers and energy infrastructure, sectors where location decisions carry long-term cost and resilience consequences. artigo.texto: CATL's Aviation Battery Exclusive Lands as JPMorgan Trims Targets on Cost Pass-Through Published on 11/15/2026 at 13:41 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has locked in a sole-supplier role for electric aviation, but the deal flow did nothing to shift JPMorgan's more cautious arithmetic on the battery maker's shares. The Chinese group on Thursday sealed a strategic partnership with Yiwite (Hangzhou) Aviation Technology, making it the exclusive battery supplier for that company's passenger and cargo eVTOL aircraft. The arrangement covers electrically powered vertical take-off and landing vehicles. It was the third leg of a busy week of alliances. On Wednesday, CATL agreed with the Civil Aviation University of China to set up a joint innovation laboratory focused on airworthiness of aviation batteries. The lab will study standards and conformity testing and build out a test platform. Two days earlier, the company signed separate strategic agreements with the public transport operators of Benxi, Changzhou, Guiyang and Lanzhou. Those cover battery supply and replacement, customer service, urban battery-swap networks, recycling and vehicle-to-grid interaction. The same day brought a memorandum with the Chenzhou city government on green resources, renewable power, swap infrastructure and transport electrification. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? JPMorgan Cuts Both Targets JPMorgan lowered its price target on CATL's H-shares to HKD420 from HKD440 on November 6, keeping a "Neutral" rating. For the A-shares, the bank trimmed its target to RMB300 from RMB310 while staying "Overweight." The driver, according to the US house, was a harder-than-expected pass-through of battery control costs. JPMorgan cut its per-unit profit assumptions rather than its volume forecasts. Market Anxiety Beyond the Model Broader worries are also weighing on the stock. The South China Morning Post attributed recent weakness to concerns over the domestic battery market, potential new US import restrictions and overcapacity, citing analysts who called for stronger measures to counter the pressure on the business. On Friday the shares fell 1.0% to CNY237.70. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. CATL's deal-making stretched into other areas as well. A November 8 cooperation with Chinalco spans non-ferrous metal materials, recycled metals, renewable energy and storage, along with support for global supply chains. For European home storage, CATL, Octopus Energy and Ampace announced a letter of intent on November 3. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 15 November Fresh CATL information released. artigo.texto: Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), Vikram Solar, Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies and Exide Energy Solutions are among 22 companies that have submitted bids for 10 GWh of advanced chemistry cell (ACC) manufacturing capacity earmarked for grid-scale energy storage applications under the government's production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme. The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has received 22 bids under the global tender for setting up giga-scale ACC manufacturing facilities in the country, marking a step towards expanding domestic battery manufacturing capabilities.The 10 GWh capacity, earmarked for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage (GSSS) applications, forms a part of the overall targeted 50 GWh ACC manufacturing capacity under the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage.Other bidders include ACME Solar Holdings, Avaada Electro, Fujiyama Power Systems, JSW Neo Energy, Megha Engineering and Infrastructures, Waaree Energy Storage Solutions, Godawari New Energy, Renew Photovoltaics and Sun Drops Energia.The list of bidders also includes GK Energy, JPM Energy Solutions, Lineage Power, Mahendra Sponge and Power, Nsure Reliable Power Solutions, Sai Bioenergy, Shirdi Sai Electricals and Utex New Energy, among others.The Request for Proposal (RFP) was floated on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal on July 15, 2026, while the pre-bid conference was held on July 29. The last date for submission of bids was November 10, and the technical bids were opened on November 11 in the presence of bidders at the Ministry of Heavy Industries.The bidding is being conducted online through a transparent two-stage Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) mechanism, the ministry said in an official statement on Thursday.In May 2021, the Union Cabinet had approved the PLI scheme for the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage, with a total budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore to achieve 50 GWh of ACC manufacturing capacity in the country.Of the targeted 50 GWh capacity, 40 GWh has already been awarded to beneficiary firms in two rounds, according to an earlier government disclosure.The scheme aims to enhance domestic ACC manufacturing capabilities and encourage large domestic and international players to establish a globally competitive battery manufacturing ecosystem in India.The 10 GWh allocation for grid-scale stationary storage is expected to support the country's growing energy storage requirements amid the expansion of renewable energy capacity. It is also aimed at strengthening energy security and strengthening the domestic value chain for ACC technologies.The strong participation in the tender reflects growing industry interest in India's ACC manufacturing potential, the Heavy Industries Ministry said. - Energy - 2 min Read RIL, Vikram Solar among 22 bidders for 10 GWh battery storage capacity under PLI scheme The 10 GWh capacity, earmarked for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage (GSSS) applications, forms a part of the overall targeted 50 GWh ACC manufacturing capacity under the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage. - Published On Nov 14, 2026 at 08:35 AM IST Comments What are your thoughts?

artigo.texto: Dubai, United Arab Emirates – Trina Storage, a global leader in energy storage solutions, has once again been recognized on the BloombergNEF (BNEF) Energy Storage Tier 1 List for Q4 2026, marking its 12th consecutive inclusion on the prestigious ranking and completing three consecutive years of Tier 1 recognition. This achievement further reinforces the company's position as a trusted and bankable partner for utility-scale energy storage projects worldwide. The latest BNEF Tier 1 Energy Storage ranking reflects the growing maturity of the global energy storage market and introduces updated assessment criteria with a stronger focus on project financing and bankability. Under the revised methodology, manufacturers are required to demonstrate successful deployment and financing track records through independently financed utility-scale projects. Trina Storage's continued presence on the list highlights the company's proven capability to deliver high-quality, financeable energy storage solutions at scale. "We are honored to be recognized by BloombergNEF for the 12th consecutive quarter," said Mr. Yang Bao, President of Energy Storage Division at Trinasolar. “The evolution of BNEF’s methodology reflects the increasing maturity of the energy storage industry. As customers place greater emphasis on project execution, financing readiness and long-term performance, we remain focused on delivering solutions that create lasting value throughout the project lifecycle.” As solar generation expands across the Middle East and Africa, battery storage can help utilities maintain grid stability and make solar power available after sunset. In Aswan, Egypt, Trina Storage supplied its Elementa 2 system as the exclusive energy storage partner for AMEA Power’s 300 MWh Abydos battery energy storage project, part of Egypt’s first utility-scale solar-plus-storage facility. Trina Storage completed installation and grid connection in 60 days, ahead of schedule. “The next phase of energy storage in the Middle East and Africa will be defined by the ability to deploy at scale while meeting increasingly demanding technical and operational requirements,” said Jack Chen, Head of Energy Storage, MEA Region at Trinasolar. “At Trina Storage, we continue to expand our portfolio with advanced, integrated solutions designed for a range of applications. Our focus is on giving utilities and developers the performance, reliability and flexibility they need for their projects.” The company’s Elementa battery energy storage system incorporates liquid-cooling architecture and advanced battery management technologies designed to support reliable operation across a range of utility-scale applications. Meanwhile, the recently introduced Elementa + Electra integrated DC+AC solution combines high-density battery storage with advanced power conversion technology, simplifying deployment while enhancing system performance and project value. The solution supports demanding utility-scale applications with features including grid-forming capability, black-start functionality, and flexible power control. As the global energy storage industry enters a new phase of growth, Trina Storage will continue to work closely with utilities and developers across the Middle East and Africa to deliver safe, reliable and high-performance solutions that maximize project value and support a more sustainable energy future. About Trina Storage Trina Storage, a business unit of Trinasolar established in 2015, is a global leader in energy storage products and solutions, dedicated to transforming the way we provide energy. Our mission is to lead the renewable energy transition through cost-competitive storage and to provide Solar for Everyone by expanding solar generation at scale. Leveraging decades of expertise in solar manufacturing, we offer cost-effective and flexible storage solutions to meet the diverse needs of our global customers. For media inquiries please contact: Mariam Agag - PR Manager, Trinasolar MEA Email: mariam.agag@trinasolar.com Lojayne Mohsen - Senior Consultant, Fekra Communications Email: lojayne.mohsen@fekracomms.com

artigo.texto: The global battery energy storage system (BESS) market is entering 2027 with intensifying competition among Sungrow, Tesla Energy, CATL, BYD, Fluence, Envision Energy and Trina Storage. Utility-scale developers are evaluating suppliers based on commissioned projects, battery costs, grid-forming technology, software capabilities, delivery schedules and long-term performance guarantees. According to Wood Mackenzie’s 2026 global BESS integrator ranking, Sungrow secured first position, followed by Tesla, CATL and BYD. Envision Energy and Trina Storage shared fifth position. Fluence, LG Energy Solution, Canadian Solar and Wärtsilä completed the top ten. The ranking evaluates AC-integrated storage solutions, including technology, safety and financial strength. Five additional companies have been selected for their technology, project references and market opportunities. Top 15 BESS Integrators: Projects, Achievements and Customer Strategies 1. Sungrow: Large-Scale Project Execution Sungrow leads through its PowerTitan storage platform, integrated power conversion systems and utility-scale execution capabilities. Its 350 MW/1,243 MWh Hams Hall project in the UK reached commercial operation in November 2026, with the first phase achieving operation within 20 days after grid connection. Sungrow also commissioned a 150 MW/600 MWh storage project in Nova Zagora, Bulgaria, in June 2026. Sungrow’s customer-winning strategy combines integrated equipment, faster commissioning, grid-support capabilities and reduced coordination requirements for developers. 2. Tesla Energy: Megapack Manufacturing and Software Tesla Energy competes through Megapack battery systems, Autobidder trading software and vertically integrated manufacturing. Tesla reports more than 77 GWh of operational deployments across over 65 countries and approximately 80 GWh of annual factory production capacity. Its customer strategy emphasizes standardized Megapack installations, automated energy trading, software optimization and long-term maintenance. Tesla’s hardware-software combination appeals to utilities and independent power producers seeking fewer integration interfaces. 3. CATL: Battery Manufacturing and Eight-Hour Storage CATL leverages its battery manufacturing scale, TENER storage platform and long-duration technology. Its EnerQB technology targets eight-hour storage applications. CATL’s October 2026 announcements concerning Quinbrook involve a 3 GW/24 GWh Australian development framework, rather than completed installations. CATL competes through cell manufacturing economics, energy density, long-duration solutions and supply agreements with major developers. 4. BYD: Vertical Integration and Project Supply BYD combines battery cell production, storage systems and manufacturing capabilities. Its battery supply relationship with Grenergy’s Oasis de Atacama development in Chile demonstrates its participation in large-scale solar-plus-storage projects. BYD targets customers seeking competitive battery pricing, integrated supply chains and large-volume procurement. However, battery supply contracts should not be confused with complete AC-system integration or EPC responsibility. 5. Envision Energy: Renewable Energy and Digital Integration Envision Energy integrates storage with renewable generation, digital energy management and grid technologies. Its 193 MW/386 MWh Neuilly-en-Thelle project in France entered construction in 2026, with operation targeted before spring 2028. Envision’s customer acquisition strategy emphasizes renewable-storage integration, digital optimization and grid-support services for utilities and project developers. 6. Trina Storage: Solar Customer Relationships Trina Storage is expanding its battery storage business using its established solar industry relationships. Its 40 MW/160.48 MWh Gamma project in Romania combines Elementa battery storage with Electra AC equipment. Installation and delivery activities were underway in 2026. Trina targets solar developers seeking hybrid generation and storage projects, integrated procurement and fewer technology interfaces. 7. Fluence: Software, Backlog and Utility Customers Fluence differentiates itself through storage integration, energy management software and utility-scale project delivery. As of June 30, 2026, Fluence reported 19.3 GWh of deployed storage, a 12.6 GW backlog and a 45.6 GW pipeline. It introduced its 10 MWh Smartstack platform in June 2026. Fluence’s customer strategy focuses on software optimization, modular systems, grid services and long-term lifecycle support. Its investor disclosures provide additional information on deployments and commercial commitments. 8. LG Energy Solution: Battery Technology and Supply Security LG Energy Solution competes through battery manufacturing, energy storage products and established customer relationships. Its strengths include cell engineering, manufacturing expertise and battery supply capabilities. Its commercial scope varies between cell supply and broader storage-system offerings. Customers should verify whether contracts cover batteries, PCS, energy management, commissioning and lifecycle warranties. 9. Canadian Solar e-STORAGE: Project Pipeline and Integration Canadian Solar’s e-STORAGE business combines battery storage systems with renewable energy project experience. At June 30, 2026, Canadian Solar disclosed an 84.1 GWh storage pipeline, 4.378 GWh backlog and 600 MWh under construction. Its competitive strategy combines integrated storage equipment, solar-plus-storage relationships and project delivery capabilities. Developers should distinguish contracted backlog from prospective pipeline opportunities. 10. Wartsila / Valo: Grid Software and Energy Optimization Wartsila established its BESS position through GEMS energy management software and utility-scale integration. artigo.texto: Masauni commends NCMC, CRDB For carbon market partnership ANTALYA, Turkey: MINISTER of State in the Vice-President’s Office, Engineer Hamad Masauni, has commended the National Carbon Monitoring Centre (NCMC) and CRDB Bank Plc for entering into a partnership aimed at strengthening Tanzania’s carbon market and attracting green investments. Speaking during the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the two institutions in Antalya, Turkey, Masauni said the collaboration would combine NCMC’s expertise in coordinating and overseeing carbon trading activities with CRDB Bank’s financial services and investment capacity. He said the partnership would create an enabling environment for financing and implementing viable carbon projects, contributing to the growth of the country’s carbon market. Masauni urged the two institutions to ensure the collaboration delivers tangible economic, social and environmental benefits to Tanzanians, including job creation, improved livelihoods, technology adoption and increased community participation in the green economy. He further challenged CRDB Bank to develop innovative financial solutions to improve access to capital for carbon project developers and other stakeholders in the sector. The minister stressed that all carbon projects must comply with the Environmental Management Act and the Environmental Management (Control and Management of Carbon Trading) Regulations, 2022, as amended in 2023. He cautioned that access to financing should not be considered authorisation to implement projects without observing legal procedures and obtaining approval from relevant authorities. Masauni said the government would continue strengthening institutional and regulatory frameworks to ensure transparency, accountability and environmental integrity in carbon trading, while ensuring the sector delivers shared benefits to the country and its people.

artigo.texto: Floating data centers could help build resilient digital infrastructure in new environments and beyond traditional locations. ABB and Hanwha Ocean have signed an MOU to advance power and control technologies for floating data centers, combining Hanwha Ocean’s offshore design and construction expertise with ABB’s electrification, automation and data center power capabilities. Through May 2027, the companies will explore power system design and operational control technologies suited to the marine environment. This includes assessing power system reliability and quality, and developing control logic to support efficient operations as computing demand changes. The collaboration will also explore how LNG engines and electrical systems can respond to changing data center power demands, helping advance reliable and resilient power solutions for floating data centers.Together, ABB and Hanwha Ocean are combining engineering expertise and power systems know-how to help build the foundations for future marine digital infrastructure. Floating data centers are data centers built on offshore floating platforms, equipped with servers, power systems, and cooling facilities. As the demand for data processing surges, land-based data centers face numerous constraints regarding site selection and power supply; consequently, floating data centers are gaining increasing attention as an alternative solution.

artigo.texto: Locally produced LFP prismatic SBB 2.0 to spearhead North American push World's first LSFT-certified UPS battery solution makes its debut Samsung SDI is set to accelerate its push into the North American market by unveiling a broad lineup of next-generation battery solutions in the United States. The company announced Sunday that it will participate in RE+ (Renewable Energy Plus) 2026 — North America's largest energy industry exhibition — which opens Tuesday (local time) in Las Vegas for a three-day run. Under the slogan "AI imagines it, batteries make it real," Samsung SDI will showcase a battery total solution lineup aimed at leading the North American market, including its ESS solution Samsung Battery Box (SBB), a high-output prismatic battery solution for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, and a high-output cylindrical battery for battery backup units (BBU). The SBB 2.0 — which drew recognition for its technological innovation when it debuted last year — serves as the flagship model for Samsung SDI's North American ESS push. The company said it has recently completed the buildout of a local production system and will begin full-scale supply. The SBB is a power-grid ESS battery solution that installs battery cells and safety devices inside a 20-foot container, optimizing customer convenience and performance. It is equipped with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. Samsung SDI applied differentiated materials and electrode technology to its proprietary prismatic form factor, significantly improving safety and longevity. Also making its North American debut is the U8A3, a prismatic battery solution for UPS systems that recently became the world's first to satisfy all criteria of the Indoor Large-Scale Fire Test (LSFT) administered by global safety certification body UL Solutions. The U8A3 uses lithium manganese oxide (LMO) prismatic battery cells and achieves industry-leading safety through multi-layered safety design across every stage — cell, module and rack. It can also respond effectively to sudden fluctuations in power load, such as the sharp spikes and drops in electricity consumption seen in AI data centers. In addition, a cylindrical battery lineup for BBU applications — combining high output and high capacity — will be on display. Visitors will be able to review Samsung SDI's product portfolio, which spans high-nickel NCA to LFP chemistries, backed by technology and reliability built up since the company began supplying battery solutions for data centers in 2017. "We will present locally tailored products and technology targeting the rapidly growing US market," a Samsung SDI official said. "Our strategy is to lead the North American market with technology purpose-built for the AI era." Meanwhile, Samsung SDI is also expanding its footprint in the electric vehicle battery market, having recently been selected as a new cell supplier for BMW's sixth-generation battery while strengthening partnerships with global EV manufacturers. likehyo85@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: MOUs signed with GGGI, ICVCM; ministry says GVCM issuance body to be established next year Eight countries, including Singapore, have expressed their intent to join the Global Verified Carbon Market (GVCM), a high-integrity carbon market initiative led by South Korea. With the latest additions, the total number of signatories to the GVCM cooperation letter of intent stands at nine: South Korea, the Dominican Republic, Morocco, Burkina Faso, Sri Lanka, Singapore, Uganda, Côte d'Ivoire and Paraguay. According to the Ministry of Economy and Finance on Sunday, the nine countries signed the joint cooperation letter of intent on Saturday (local time) at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, held in Antalya, Turkey. The GVCM is a multilateral carbon market framework the government is developing to provide common carbon credit issuance standards and infrastructure that multiple countries can use jointly to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Companies will be able to use the framework to pursue greenhouse gas reduction projects in developing countries, generate carbon credits and trade them on international carbon markets. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Lee Hyung-il said in a video opening address that the GVCM is "a platform built together by reflecting the diverse experiences and development needs of participating countries," adding that it "carries great significance as a new multilateral model in which three or more countries participate simultaneously — not a bilateral arrangement." The ministry also signed a trilateral memorandum of understanding with the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) and the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market (ICVCM) to enhance the credibility and quality of the GVCM. The three organizations will pursue knowledge sharing on Core Carbon Principles (CCPs) and provide education and training for GVCM participating countries to improve the market's quality. Moon Ji-seong, director general for international economic affairs at the ministry, said the MOU signing was an opportunity to raise the quality of the GVCM by sharing ICVCM's expertise and experience. The ministry said it plans to complete the establishment of the GVCM issuance body next year and will work to bring in more countries, international organizations and private institutions going forward. oskymoon@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: SK Telecom said Monday it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Hyosung Heavy Industries to cooperate on developing gigawatt-scale AI data centers. The two companies will work on securing key equipment for 345-kilovolt substations, testing 800-volt direct-current power distribution technology and identifying new data center projects. Under the agreement, SK Telecom will contribute its AI data center development and operational expertise, while Hyosung Heavy Industries will provide its power infrastructure manufacturing and engineering capabilities. The companies will coordinate supply plans for major equipment, including transformers, to prevent procurement delays from affecting construction schedules. They will also jointly review and test 800V DC distribution, which can reduce power conversion stages and improve data center energy efficiency. They also plan to share expertise in operating and maintaining ultra-high-voltage substations to improve power supply stability and reliability once data centers are operational. The partnership will eventually extend to AI data center development and construction, with both companies seeking new business opportunities and joint business models. "This partnership will help secure the core power infrastructure needed for AI data centers and expand into cooperation on developing and building large-scale facilities," SK Telecom CEO Jung Jai-hun said. "We will strengthen our capabilities in gigawatt-scale AI data center development and take a leading role in the global AI infrastructure market." Hyosung Heavy Industries CEO Woo Tae-hee said the agreement would combine the company's power technology with SK Telecom's data center expertise to establish a stable foundation for electricity supply. jyoungseon8@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: LS Electric, a South Korean electrical equipment manufacturer, said Monday it secured a $93.83 million contract to supply power distribution systems for a hyper-scale artificial intelligence data center in the US. Under the agreement, the company will deliver 38-kilovolt high-voltage switchgear and low-voltage switchgear in phases to an unnamed global technology company. Switchgear controls and protects electrical circuits, helping distribute electricity safely throughout large facilities. The latest order extends LS Electric’s involvement in the client's data center project from the initial construction phase to a subsequent expansion. As AI adoption accelerates, demand for computing capacity has grown, placing greater emphasis on “time to power,” the period required for a data center to secure an operational electricity supply. To meet delivery schedules, LS Electric operates manufacturing facilities in Cheongju, South Korea, and the US states of Utah and Texas. The company said its production network enables it to meet the tight delivery timelines of data center projects. Beyond conventional alternating current (AC) distribution, the manufacturer is expanding into direct current (DC) systems, which can reduce energy losses by limiting the power conversions required to operate servers. At its Cheonan plant, LS Electric operates a DC-powered factory equipped with solid-state transformers for voltage conversion, solid-state circuit breakers for electrical protection and energy storage systems. The facility serves as a testing ground for next-generation power grids and data center applications. “The latest contract reflects the quality of our power equipment and our ability to execute projects in North America,” an LS Electric official said. “We will continue expanding our business by providing solutions tailored to the needs of major technology customers.” yejinlim@heraldcorp.com

Breaks Into the Solid-State Battery Mass-Production Market With an Order in the ₩20 Billion Range From a Global Company - Input - 2026-11-16 08:46:51 - Updated - 2026-11-16 08:49:41 [Financial News] mPlus Corp., a company specializing in rechargeable-battery assembly equipment, is stepping up its push into the next-generation battery market after securing an order worth around ₩20 billion for solid-state battery equipment from a global company. The deal is drawing attention because it marks an expansion of the company’s equipment business, previously centered on electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems (ESS), into solid-state battery mass-production processes. According to industry sources on the 16th, mPlus Corp. recently secured an order worth around ₩20 billion from a global company for solid-state battery assembly and electrode-line equipment. The equipment is expected to be used to build the global company’s solid-state battery production line. The equipment to be supplied incorporates technologies developed in-house by mPlus Corp., including notching, stacking and precision dispensing. The company is also developing Roll Press technology needed for solid-state battery manufacturing. It plans to use these technologies to expand the range of equipment it can supply for solid-state battery production. Solid-state batteries are next-generation batteries that replace liquid electrolytes with solid ones to improve safety and energy density. However, their complex manufacturing processes make securing reliable mass-production technology a key challenge for commercialization. As a result, technological competition is intensifying not only among battery manufacturers but also among makers of equipment for key manufacturing processes. With this order as a springboard, mPlus Corp. plans to focus on securing global customers and diversifying its business. It has also recently been pursuing entry into the market for defense and special-purpose battery equipment, targeting European battery companies. The strategy is to broaden its order base to include solid-state and special-purpose batteries, in addition to equipment for EVs and ESS. Industry observers expect order opportunities for related equipment makers to grow as the solid-state battery market moves beyond research and development and begins preparing for commercialization. In particular, they say that a track record of supplying initial production lines could be a factor in gauging competitiveness in future orders for mass-production facilities. A company representative said, "This order is significant because it gives us a track record of supplying a global customer in the solid-state battery assembly-equipment sector," and added, "We also expect opportunities for additional orders as our customers expand mass production." Meanwhile, mPlus Corp. is expanding its business portfolio to include pouch-type, prismatic and solid-state battery assembly equipment, as well as autonomous mobile robots (AIMR) and control systems. artigo.texto: Samsung SDI to supply LFP batteries to Jupiter Power SEOUL, Nov. 16 (Yonhap) -- Samsung SDI Co., South Korea's second-largest battery maker, said Monday its U.S. subsidiary has secured a deal estimated to be worth trillions of won to supply lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries to a U.S. energy storage company. Samsung SDI America signed a three-year, 16-gigawatt-hour (GWh) battery supply agreement with Jupiter Power, a U.S. energy storage system (ESS) developer owned by BlackRock, the South Korean company said in a press release. Under the agreement, Samsung SDI will supply LFP batteries for Jupiter Power's ESS, with deliveries scheduled to begin in 2029. Combined with an earlier agreement, the latest deal brings Samsung SDI's cumulative orders from Jupiter Power to about 27 GWh. The batteries will be manufactured at StarPlus Energy, a U.S. joint venture between Samsung SDI and Stellantis NV, in the U.S. state of Indiana. Jupiter Power, owned by U.S. asset management giant BlackRock, is one of the largest developers and operators of energy storage projects in the United States. The contract comes shortly after Samsung SDI began mass production of LFP batteries at the Indiana facility. Industry observers said the deal could help Samsung SDI gain a foothold in the ESS battery market, which has long been dominated by Chinese manufacturers, by leveraging its U.S. production capabilities and non-Chinese supply chain. artigo.texto: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. The Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) has become one of the founding members of the Global Carbon Market Network, a new international platform established with the support of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), according to the AIFC. The initiative was announced at the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye. It aims to strengthen links between carbon and financial markets, improve transparency and trust, and facilitate cross-border transactions. The network's founding members also include organizations from Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe and Latin America, such as Climate Impact X, Johannesburg Stock Exchange, Indonesia Stock Exchange, Global Carbon Council, Verra and Voluntary Carbon Market Company. On the sidelines of COP31, AIFC also organized an expert discussion titled “Voluntary Carbon Market: Infrastructure, Standards and Financing.” The session brought together representatives of international organizations, carbon market infrastructure providers, financial institutions and the private sector. Participants discussed practical mechanisms for advancing climate finance and voluntary carbon markets in Central Asia, including green and sustainable finance, ESG instruments, development bank funding, voluntary carbon market mechanisms and International Renewable Energy Certificates (I-REC). They also examined investor requirements for climate projects, ways to structure projects to attract capital, and opportunities to develop demand for carbon credits and I-REC certificates in the region. “For the voluntary carbon market to become a fully fledged source of financing for climate projects, generating carbon credits alone is not enough. What is needed is an integrated ecosystem comprising high-quality projects, internationally recognized standards, transparent infrastructure, access to capital and sustainable buyer demand. For Central Asia, it is particularly important to connect climate projects with financial markets and establish clear mechanisms for investors," said Zhanbolat Kakishev, Chief Product Officer of the AIFC Authority. He added that the AIFC was ready to support Kazakhstan's efforts to develop a portfolio of climate investment projects by providing financial infrastructure, international expertise and access to investors and market participants. The AIFC said it would continue supporting sustainable finance, international cooperation and the development of an ecosystem for climate projects in Kazakhstan and Central Asia.

artigo.texto: Data centers tiveram ampla derrota nas eleições de meio de mandato dos EUA. Foto: Dado Galdieri/Bloomberg Indústrias e ativistas imaginam que parte da capacidade planejada para estados americanos possa vir parar em território brasileiro Bruno Romani Repórter de tecnologia O “tsunami azul” que varreu Donald Trump nas eleições de meio de mandato dos EUA foi também um grande plebiscito sobre inteligência artificial (IA), com candidatos favoráveis à regulação — e opositores dos grandes bilionários do setor — conseguindo ampla votação. Mais especificamente, as urnas deram um grande recado sobre o que a população de lá pensa da presença de data centers em suas comunidades. Agora, indústria e ativistas imaginam que parte dessa demanda possa vir parar no Brasil — para o bem e para o mal. Vale lembrar que o processo eleitoral americano não escolheu apenas novos membros do Legislativo federal e dos Executivos estaduais. Houve também referendos sobre diversos temas, entre eles a paralisação ou a restrição de data centers em vários condados do país. A rejeição foi ampla: segundo a consultoria Redbud, dos 47 referendos, 44 tiveram resultado negativo para o setor e apenas um foi favorável (outros dois ainda não têm resultado). O Goldman Sachs alertou os investidores de que o resultado poderia afetar 45% da expansão de capacidade planejada para o território americano — se isso acontecer, a própria expansão da indústria da IA fica em xeque e começa a se formar um clima terrível de bolha. Na semana passada, essa simples perspectiva fez as empresas de tecnologia perderem US$ 2,5 trilhões em valor de mercado. Elon Musk correu para o X: “Os data centers no espaço parecem bastante atraentes no momento”. Ele, claro, já está fazendo propaganda de um potencial serviço que a SpaceX pode oferecer. Mas nem é preciso ir tão longe: o Brasil já aparece como opção. Sérgio Sgobbi, diretor de relações institucionais e governamentais da Associação das Empresas de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação (Brasscom), me explicou o que coloca o país em jogo: O cenário nos EUA cria uma oportunidade para o Brasil. Lá, criou-se uma resistência muito forte a data centers, mais por questões econômicas do que ambientais, reflexo da demanda por energia. A gente tem uma matriz diversa. A outra característica é a interligação. A gente tem problemas de distribuição, mas tem uma capacidade interligada que outros países não têm. A Brasscom previa que o Brasil receberia US$ 92 bilhões em investimentos acumulados em equipamentos de TI até 2031 — e o tamanho do bolo é maior, porque a conta não considera custos de construção e de infraestrutura física de suporte, como geradores, sistemas de ar-condicionado/refrigeração, sistemas de combate a incêndio, baterias e no-breaks. Sgobbi admite que a entidade pode voltar à prancheta para refazer as contas após as eleições americanas. Ainda não é possível saber qual será o novo número. Na semana passada, Marcos Peigo, CEO da Scala, disse ao jornal Valor Econômico que o Brasil está diante de uma oportunidade de US$ 500 bilhões. Já o representante da Brasscom tenta dar uma ideia de outra forma. Ele afirma que os aportes em hardware, redes e data centers para IA equivaleram a 1,5% do PIB dos EUA no 1º trimestre de 2026 (contra uma média histórica de 0,7% entre 2015 e 2022). É claro que não haverá transferência automática de toda essa capacidade para o Brasil, mas uma fração disso já significaria valores históricos para o país. Victor Arnaud, presidente da Equinix no Brasil, lembra que o país não é o destino natural da demanda expulsa dos EUA. O norte da Europa, por exemplo, tem mais capacidade instalada do que toda a América Latina — o Google decidiu investir € 13 bilhões na Finlândia. A gigante também anunciou outros US$ 15 bilhões para a Malásia em 2027 e 2028, uma clara indicação de que o Sudeste Asiático também está na fila do pão. E há ainda os rivais locais na América do Sul, cada um com seus atrativos e problemas. A Argentina tem a amizade entre Milei e Trump e o frio da Patagônia (vale lembrar, porém, que um suposto projeto da OpenAI por lá está parado); o Paraguai tem Itaipu e um regramento mais relaxado (mas também uma crise política profunda); e o Chile tem o seu histórico no setor (e um movimento de rejeição que o acompanha). Arnaud reforça que a regulamentação do Redata, a harmonização do ICMS entre os estados e a futura aprovação do Marco da IA são reformas que viabilizam o Brasil, independentemente de onde venha a demanda por data centers. Na sexta (6), a ministra-chefe da Casa Civil, Miriam Belchior, afirmou que a regulamentação do Redata deverá ser debatida com o presidente Lula após a viagem dele à Ásia. Ainda que toda essa tramitação demore a ocorrer, o executivo da Equinix lembrou que um dos principais atrativos do Brasil permanece: O Brasil continua sendo o maior mercado da América Latina e vai continuar crescendo. O usuário daqui não vai falar que não usa mais o celular ou que gosta quando o vídeo demora para carregar. O Pix, o streaming e a vida digital já garantem o crescimento. A Equinix vinha investindo numa média de R$ 1 bilhão por ano e, nos últimos 12 meses, aumentou isso em 50%. Até aqui, com o Redata, a ideia do Brasil era trazer para o território nacional infraestrutura para reduzir o nosso déficit computacional — segundo o Ministério da Fazenda, 60% da nossa demanda roda no exterior. Então, como o país poderia surgir como opção para fornecer capacidade a outros mercados? Sgobbi diz que um data center de grande porte é construído para 100 megawatts (MW), mas costuma iniciar a operação com “apenas 5 MW e expandir conforme a venda de capacidade”. Uma eventual absorção da carga americana poderia fazer os novos data centers no país iniciarem com capacidade maior. Segundo a Bloomberg, o resultado das eleições nos EUA está fazendo a ByteDance, dona do TikTok, estudar a ampliação da capacidade de seus novos data centers no Nordeste. artigo.texto: Hungarian regulators ordered Chinese battery component manufacturer SEMCORP to halt production at its plant in Debrecen on June 24 after water samples collected at the facility showed excessive concentrations of metals and other pollutants. On July 3, authorities returned to the factory and ordered a complete shutdown of operations, this time citing violations of fire safety regulations. SEMCORP is considered the world's largest manufacturer of separator films, a critical component in lithium-ion batteries, particularly those used in electric vehicles. According to published reports, its separators are incorporated into batteries manufactured by Panasonic and CATL that are installed in electric cars. As of now, SEMCORP's Debrecen plant remains shut down. BYD promised not to pollute. Then Hungary's foreign minister went to work for the company In 2023, shortly after Chinese automaker BYD announced plans to establish its first European factory in Szeged, Hungary, a highly publicized event was held at the future plant site. Szeged Mayor László Botka and China's ambassador to Hungary, Gong Tao, emphasized that construction and operations would comply with the strictest environmental regulations. In May this year, Hungarian police opened an investigation into BYD. According to Hungary's environmental protection minister, "BYD is in a state of significant violation of the environmental protection permits it received and must immediately cease its polluting activities." Not long afterward, it emerged that Péter Szijjártó, who served as Hungary's foreign minister during the establishment of BYD's factory, had been appointed this year to head the company's foreign relations and investment operations. SEMCORP and BYD are far from alone. Chinese battery manufacturer CATL has established a factory in Debrecen with an investment of 7.3 billion euros and is preparing to expand it. Samsung operates a factory near the town of Göd, built with an investment of 1.5 billion euros. South Korea's SK has a battery factory near Komárom, established with an investment of 3.3 billion euros. EVE Energy has a factory in Debrecen built with an investment of 1.3 billion euros, while ECOPRO has established another facility in the city with an investment of 830 million euros. Chinese battery manufacturer SUNWODA also has a plant in Nyíregyháza, where total investment is expected to reach 1.5 billion euros upon completion, according to local reports. An automotive manufacturing powerhouse since the 1990s Why do battery manufacturers prefer to establish factories in Hungary? The first reason concerns European Union taxation policy. When it comes to vehicles manufactured outside Europe, as well as those assembled in Europe by non-European automakers, the EU considers not only where a vehicle was assembled but also how much of its value was produced within Europe. In an electric vehicle, the battery accounts for a substantial portion of the vehicle's value. If the battery is manufactured in China, the vehicle could face significant tariffs. Hungary is also relatively close to the centers of Europe's automotive industry, allowing manufacturers to transport components by rail to vehicle assembly plants in the Czech Republic and Germany. In an industry where only a few hours may separate battery production from installation in a vehicle, that proximity offers a considerable advantage. But there is another reason: Hungary has a long automotive manufacturing tradition, and vehicles produced there can even be found on Israeli roads. As early as 1893, two Hungarian inventors, János Csonka and Donát Bánki, patented a carburetor, a component that remained essential to passenger vehicles until the 1980s. After decades of communist rule, Hungary began attracting foreign automakers. Suzuki established a factory in the country in 1991, producing vehicles that were also exported to Israel. Audi followed a year later. Last year, approximately 411,000 vehicles were manufactured in Hungary, compared with about 437,000 in 2024 and 507,000 in 2023. The country's automotive industry employs approximately 150,000 production workers. But the reliance on automakers that has supported Hungary's economy since the 1990s has also exposed it to difficulties facing manufacturers in recent years. Mercedes-Benz, Audi and Suzuki are confronting challenges in the global automotive market, particularly growing competition from Chinese automakers. Still, if European countries offer incentives for vehicles whose batteries are also manufactured in Europe, why has Greece not become a battery manufacturing powerhouse? Why not Austria or Germany? That brings us to the second reason Hungary became an attractive destination for battery manufacturers: Viktor Orbán, whose government collapsed this year. Orbán was responsible for bringing battery manufacturers to Hungary. As early as 2010, he announced a policy known as Keleti Nyitás, or "Eastern Opening." Orbán recognized that the world's emerging economic power was no longer concentrated in Europe and understood that the future of the automotive industry lay in electric vehicles. The basic principles of the Eastern Opening policy centered on commitments from major energy companies in China, Japan and South Korea to invest approximately $20 billion in Hungary over a decade. In return, the Hungarian government offered battery manufacturers generous subsidies and tax exemptions. The problem, according to reports in Hungary, was that tax exemptions were not the only concessions the manufacturers received. Hungarian media reports have described serious environmental damage, groundwater contamination and the construction of factories near residential areas. Those concerns prompted residents of Debrecen, Hungary's second-largest city, to stage heated demonstrations last year against the expansion of battery factories in the area. artigo.texto: Data Centers DID YOU KNOW? the Potomac River basin has the largest concentration of data centers in the world. Most of which are nestled in Northern Virginia, now known as “Data Center Alley” – a mega hub of data center infrastructure estimated to handle 70% of all global internet traffic. Northern Virginia is home to one of the world’s largest clusters of data centers. And as more facilities are proposed across the Potomac watershed, there’s a question worth asking: What does all this growth mean for the rivers, streams, and drinking water we depend on? Every time we stream a show, store a photo, or use an AI tool, data centers help make it possible. These large facilities house the computers that keep our digital lives running. But they also need electricity, cooling, and land. Their effects on water vary widely depending on how and where they are built—and with so many projects on the horizon, we need to look at the bigger picture. A data center is an industrial facility that houses expansive, high-powered computing equipment to continuously store and process data for users globally. An average AI data center contains 200,000 computer servers, miles of wiring, batteries, water systems, hundreds of air conditioning units, and is supported by dozens of high-powered, industrial backup diesel generators. Data centers operate constantly, using massive amounts of water in order to cool and power their systems. In our region, they draw this water from Potomac-fed water supplies. This is especially important during the hottest days of the year, when data center water demand spikes at the most water-stressed time of year. Why This Matters for the Potomac and Shenandoah Rivers Data center proposals are multiplying across our region. AI is helping drive that growth, though not every proposed project will necessarily be built. What happens next matters: choices about water use, wastewater, construction, and power infrastructure can shape the health of the Potomac and Shenandoah for years to come. The Potomac River watershed remains a legacy hub and now has more than 350 operating data centers and is projected to surpass 1,000 – placing 200 million square feet of buildings on roughly 20,000 acres of land. Because of the unprecedented construction of these facilities in our watershed, the exact impacts on the environment and water quality remain unclear. However, the primary concerns associated with data centers include: - Water drawdowns - Periodic cooling system discharge - Increased polluted runoff - Construction site pollution - Threats from fuel spills - Threats to drinking water intakes - Risk of substation fires - Toxic e-waste in landfills - Developments on toxic sites - Impacts from power line construction - Power plant operation threats Rapid data center expansion helped the Potomac River earn the title of America’s Most Endangered River in 2026. How PRKN is taking action The extent of data center impacts on river systems and waterways is still not fully understood, and comprehensive analyses and assessments are needed to begin to grasp their effects on our rivers. What we do know is that when unchecked, these installations can pose serious risks to the watershed and the primary clean drinking water source for six million people in the Potomac River basin. PRKN is keeping a watchful eye on the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers for data center impacts and fighting for adequacy of state permitting, such as for cooling system releases, and will call for more public stream monitoring on tributaries where high concentrations of these facilities are upstream from drinking water intakes. Importantly, PRKN will be a voice to ensure that clean water protections are seriously managed in data center development.

artigo.texto: An aerial view of the world's first 300-megawatt artificial-cavern compressed air energy storage power station, Yuanchu No 1, in Northwest China's Gansu Province. Photo: CCTV News The world's first 300-megawatt artificial-cavern compressed air energy storage (CAES) power station has been connected to the grid in Northwest China's Gansu Province, marking a major step in bringing the technology from experimental testing to large-scale engineering applications, CCTV News reported on Monday, citing China Energy Engineering Corporation (China Energy). The project, known as Yuanchu No 1, provides a new engineering example for diversifying China's compressed air energy storage technologies. The station has four air-storage caverns excavated in rock formations about 110 meters underground. It is equipped with a 300-MW generating unit and has an energy storage capacity of 1,800 megawatt-hours. With a round-trip efficiency of 72 percent, the facility can generate electricity continuously for six hours on a single discharge and has a projected annual power output of 600 million kilowatt-hours. Compressed air energy storage works by converting electricity into energy stored in compressed air, which can later be converted back into electricity when needed. Artificially excavated hard-rock caverns offer an alternative to natural underground storage spaces such as salt caverns. Suitable rock formations are more widely distributed, allowing greater flexibility in site selection, although construction costs are relatively high, according to a report by China Electric Power News published on the website of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Engineering Thermophysics. The report noted that suitable salt formations are concentrated in parts of central, eastern and southern China, while the country's northern regions, which have extensive wind and solar power installations and strong demand for large-scale energy storage, lack suitable geological conditions for salt cavern storage. The Gansu project reached a key testing milestone in September, when an initial air-injection test at its No. 4 underground storage cavern succeeded, with pressure reaching 12.63 mega-pascals, setting a record for compressed air storage in large artificial caverns, according to China Energy. The grid connection comes amid rapid growth in China's new energy storage sector. The country's installed new energy storage capacity reached 136 million kilowatts by the end of 2025, up 84 percent from a year earlier, according to the National Energy Administration (NEA). Lithium-ion batteries accounted for 96.1 percent of the total, while compressed air storage, flow batteries, flywheels and other technologies made up the remaining 3.9 percent. Energy storage projects with a duration of four hours or longer accounted for 27.6 percent of total installed capacity, up about 12 percentage points from the end of 2024, the NEA said. China is also seeking to diversify its energy storage technologies under its development plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). The plan, jointly issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and the NEA, sets a target of 300 million kilowatts of installed new energy storage capacity by 2030, with an average storage duration of about three hours. artigo.texto: CHINA / SOCIETY China to boost new types of energy storage during 2026-2030 By Xinhua Published: Nov 14, 2026 09:01 AM China will accelerate the development of new types of energy storage during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to support the building of a new electric power system, according to a plan released on Friday. The plan, issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and the National Energy Administration (NEA), sets a target of 300 million kilowatts of installed new types of energy storage by 2030, with an average storage duration of about three hours. It also aims to shift the sector from large-scale expansion to market-driven growth. New types of energy storage refer to energy storage technologies other than pumped-storage hydropower, mainly including electrochemical, compressed-air and gravity storage. The plan calls for new types of energy storage to participate fairly in electricity markets, and encourages renewable energy megabases equipped with storage to join cross-provincial power markets as a single entity. It also calls for a refined pricing mechanism that reflects the value of stored power, with charging and discharging prices set through fair market trading. The emphasis on market mechanisms comes as China's power market increasingly matures. Investment in new types of energy storage was initially policy-driven, relying largely on mandatory deployment rules and subsidies, but the sector is now shifting toward market-based mechanisms, Huayuan Securities said in a research report. Xu Dongjie, deputy chief engineer of the China Electric Power Planning and Engineering Institute, called the 300-million-kilowatt target a prudent, science-based minimum target that meets system needs and supports a reasonable rise in utilization while giving the industry confidence and preventing investment-driven boom-and-bust cycles. China leads the world in new types of energy storage, with installed capacity accounting for around 40 percent of the global total. By the end of 2025, China had built and put into operation 136 million kilowatts of new types of energy storage, with average storage duration reaching 2.58 hours, 0.3 hours longer than at the end of 2024, according to the NEA.

artigo.texto: [SMM PV Flash] Ecuador Applies Zero VAT and Currency Outflow Tax to Solar and Storage Equipment Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa signed Executive Decree 530, published on November 11 in the Fifth Supplement to Official Gazette No. 407, setting a 0% rate for value-added tax and the tax on foreign currency outflows (ISD) on electricity-sector equipment including solar PV and energy storage systems. A subsequent ministerial agreement, MAE-MAE-2026-0118-AM, lists 55 categories of goods eligible for the 0% VAT rate in the domestic market — solar cells, modules, inverters, power optimisers, controllers, mounting structures, trackers and DC cables — and 104 tariff subheadings eligible for the 0% ISD rate on imports, with storage goods covering stationary cells and modules, battery banks, integrated systems, bidirectional converters and battery management equipment. The new rates took effect on November 12, and the decree lets taxpayers deduct VAT paid on qualifying purchases and imports made between January 1, 2026 and entry into force as an expense for the 2026 income tax year. The measure removes import and transaction taxes on solar and storage equipment, part of Ecuador's push to accelerate private renewable investment after the 2024 supply shortfalls and blackouts.

artigo.texto: A new legislative review estimates that Virginia’s data center tax break generated 22 cents in state tax revenue for every dollar companies saved. Staff for the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission presented the findings Monday. The report estimates that data centers saved an average of $811.5 million a year from fiscal 2021 through 2025. Researchers estimated that the business activity the tax break attracted generated $179.4 million a year in state taxes, leaving a difference of $632.1 million a year. The revenue estimate excludes local taxes, including property taxes that cities and counties collect from data centers. The exemption lets qualifying data center operators and tenants buy computer equipment and software without paying sales and use tax. Five years of savings from that one tax break accounted for 60% of the $6.8 billion in tax breaks, grants and other business incentives the commission counted over a decade. To figure out what Virginia got back, researchers had to estimate how much data center business would have come to the state anyway. Earlier reviews assumed the tax break drove at least 90% of data center location and expansion activity in Virginia. The new review puts that share at about half. It draws on research into how sales and use tax exemptions affected the number, square footage and energy use of data centers across states. The Virginia Economic Development Partnership said in an Oct. 28 letter that the change had a substantial effect on the estimates. The partnership urged the commission to explain how much its findings depend on that assumption and to keep evaluating its method as more Virginia-specific evidence becomes available. The commission estimated that the exemption supported about 18,100 private-sector jobs a year, including jobs at businesses that supply data centers. It also estimated that the exemption added about $3.9 billion a year to Virginia’s gross domestic product over those five years. A Senate proposal to end the sales tax exemption early helped stall state budget talks this spring. Lawmakers kept the exemption in place in June and added a separate tax on electricity used by data center operators. The electricity tax took effect July 1 and runs through June 30, 2028. The state budget caps deposits from the tax into Virginia’s general fund at $600 million per fiscal year. Lawmakers are still split over the exemption. At an Oct. 26 meeting, Senate Finance Chairwoman Louise Lucas, D-Portsmouth, backed repealing it. House Appropriations Chairman Luke Torian, D-Prince William, urged the state to honor its commitments to the industry while addressing the effects of data center growth on communities. artigo.texto: By Alex Adi At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, global leaders and climate negotiators are focusing on one of the mechanisms for financing climate action: carbon credits. Under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, countries can trade emission reductions and removals through international carbon markets. But what exactly is a carbon credit, and how can Ghana position itself to turn its environmental initiatives into revenue, create jobs and build cleaner cities? A carbon credit represents one metric tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) reduced, avoided or removed from the atmosphere. For instance, when Ghana protects its forests, converts organic waste into compost instead of allowing it to decompose in landfills, or replaces diesel generators with solar power, it can reduce greenhouse gas emissions. When these reductions or removals are properly measured, independently verified and certified under an approved standard, they can generate carbon credits that are traded in the market. Companies and countries can purchase these credits to meet certain climate commitments or offset emissions, depending on the rules governing the market. In simple terms, Ghana can earn revenue by undertaking activities that reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions and selling the resulting verified credits. Ghana’s growing carbon market Ghana has established a Carbon Market Office and a framework to regulate carbon market activities and international transactions. One example of the country’s involvement in the market is the Jospong Group’s Integrated Recycling and Compost Plants. The company secured a bilateral agreement with the Swiss Government at COP28, with carbon credit transactions estimated to be worth US$20 million by 2030. Beyond waste management, Ghana is also generating carbon credits through forest conservation initiatives, including the Ghana Cocoa Forest REDD+ Programme. For a developing economy such as Ghana, the carbon market presents several potential opportunities. Revenue without additional borrowing Carbon credit transactions could provide Ghana with a source of foreign revenue and attract investment without increasing the country’s public debt. Employment opportunities Investment in reforestation, waste sorting, recycling and renewable energy could create jobs for young people, particularly in communities involved in environmental protection and sustainable resource management. Cleaner cities Carbon finance could provide additional incentives for improved municipal waste management, including recycling and composting. These activities could help reduce the volume of waste sent to landfills and ease sanitation challenges in urban communities. Supporting the energy transition Revenue from carbon credits could also support solar energy and clean cooking initiatives, helping households and businesses adopt cleaner energy sources. The need for transparency and accountability Despite the opportunities, carbon market experts have cautioned that Ghana must establish strong safeguards to ensure that the benefits are properly managed and shared. Transparency, independent verification and clear benefit-sharing arrangements are essential to preventing greenwashing and ensuring that carbon credits represent genuine emission reductions or removals. There are also concerns that communities, farmers and other groups directly involved in protecting forests and natural resources could be excluded from the financial benefits if appropriate arrangements are not put in place. For Ghana, therefore, participation in the carbon market must go beyond generating and selling credits. It must also ensure that the people and communities contributing to environmental protection receive a fair share of the proceeds. Carbon trading is not simply a form of aid or charity. It is a market that depends on credible data, proper measurement, independent verification and compliance with established standards. If Ghana strengthens its regulatory framework and ensures that the benefits are fairly distributed, its forests, waste management systems and clean energy initiatives could become valuable sources of climate finance and international investment.

artigo.texto: Md. Shahidul Haque Anralya, Turkuye. Bangladesh and Singapore have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, create new opportunities for climate finance, and promote joint initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The MoU was signed on Saturday morning (14 November) at the Singapore Pavilion during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye. Sheikh Faridul Islam, State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, signed the MoU on behalf of Bangladesh, while Melvin Ong, Secretary of Singapore's Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, signed on behalf of Singapore. The MoU marks a significant milestone in facilitating Bangladesh's effective participation in international carbon markets, expanding opportunities for carbon financing and environmentally sustainable investments, and supporting the implementation of the country's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0). Speaking at the signing ceremony, State Minister Sheikh Faridul Islam said, Bangladesh warmly welcomes this important partnership with Singapore under the Paris Agreement. This cooperation will play a significant role in unlocking new opportunities for carbon finance, developing high-quality and transparent carbon markets, and supporting the implementation of Bangladesh's NDC 3.0. Bangladesh is committed to working closely with Singapore to advance sustainable development, achieve ambitious climate goals, and strengthen effective global climate action. Under the MoU, the two countries have agreed to exchange information, knowledge, and experience related to carbon credits and strengthen future cooperation on carbon emission reduction projects based on mutual interests and benefits. This collaboration will help accelerate climate change mitigation efforts by leveraging opportunities for international cooperation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The initiative is expected to support the development of internationally recognized carbon markets in Bangladesh, facilitate the transfer of climate-friendly technologies, attract greater private sector investment, and create new opportunities for international climate finance. It will also contribute to advancing the country's sustainable and low-carbon development initiatives and achieving its national climate targets. As a follow-up to the MoU, Bangladesh and Singapore are expected to sign an Implementation Agreement at COP32, scheduled to be held in Ethiopia next year. The agreement is expected to further strengthen the effectiveness, institutional framework, and practical implementation of bilateral cooperation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.

artigo.texto: Em Belém, a instalação de um data center de R$ 250 milhões preocupa moradores de duas ocupações que enfrentam disputas por terra, falta de saneamento e incertezas sobre os impactos do empreendimento Resumo Belém deve receber, em 2027, o BEL1, um data center com investimento anunciado de R$ 250 milhões. Essas estruturas, responsáveis pelo armazenamento e processamento de grandes volumes de dados, são parte da infraestrutura que sustenta o avanço da inteligência artificial. O empreendimento é apresentado pela Elea Data Centers em parceria com a AXIA Energia, antiga Eletronorte, e está previsto para a região da Subestação Miramar II, em uma área próxima a comunidades que vivem há anos entre a falta de infraestrutura básica, a disputa pela terra e a violação de direitos humanos. A poucos minutos do local projetado para o empreendimento estão o Residencial Semente de Deus (Deus Proverá), com mais de 300 famílias ocupando a área na região da Avenida/Rodovia Arthur Bernardes, e a Comunidade Mirandinha-Miramar Shalon, ocupação que fica na região do Barreiro-Miramar, também nas proximidades da Arthur Bernardes e do Complexo Miramar. Separadas por menos de dois quilômetros, as duas ocupações ficam a aproximadamente 5 km e 6 km do centro histórico de Belém, respectivamente. Um ano após sediar a 30ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP30), a capital paraense se prepara para receber um empreendimento voltado à economia digital enquanto famílias que vivem nas proximidades da área prevista para sua instalação ainda reivindicam acesso à água, saneamento básico, moradia digna e segurança fundiária. O BEL1 ainda não aparece como objeto dos processos judiciais que envolvem as duas comunidades. No entanto, os impactos térmicos, sonoros e ambientais específicos do projeto já deveriam ter sido demonstrados por estudos e processos de licenciamento, que permanecem inexistentes. Para quem mora no Barreiro, a preocupação real chegou antes da inteligência artificial. Questionada pela Ponte sobre os impactos do empreendimento, a Elea Data Centers afirmou que o BEL1 está em fase de pré-projeto e desenvolvimento de engenharia. Segundo a empresa, os estudos em andamento orientarão o controle de ruído e a dissipação de calor. A resposta, porém, não apresenta resultados que permitam dimensionar esses possíveis impactos sobre as comunidades nem detalha a situação do licenciamento ambiental. Sobre o cronograma, a companhia disse que a previsão de início da operação depende da conclusão dessas fases (leia nota na íntegra ao final do texto). O calor, a terra e a incerteza A ocupação do Residencial Semente de Deus teve início em abril de 2022, na região do Barreiro, próxima à Baía do Guajará, onde mais de 300 famílias passaram a ocupar uma área da Avenida Arthur Bernardes, nas proximidades do centro da capital paraense. O processo judicial registra relatos de incursões policiais nos primeiros dias da ocupação. Em 26 e 28 de abril, agentes estiveram no local para exigir que moradores deixassem a área. Numa segunda ocasião, segundo os depoimentos, os policiais intensificaram a abordagem, muxando os ocupantes com uso de spray de pimenta e ameaças de acionar os agentes da Companhia de Operações Especiais (COE) e das Rondas Ostensivas Táticas Motorizadas (ROTAM). A ação policial de desocupação da área chegou a ocorrer, e houve relatos de agressões a uma mulher grávida. Quatro anos depois, a comunidade permanece no local, apesar das disputas pela terra e das tentativas de desocupação. Milson Lopes, uma das lideranças e principais referências da comunidade, fala do calor dentro de sua casa enquanto limpa o suor da testa e regula o ventilador que tenta vencer a temperatura próxima dos 39 °C. “Belém costuma ter chuva toda a tarde. Nós não estamos tendo”, comenta. Milson lembra que costumava dormir na rede durante a tarde. Hoje, por conta do calor, afirma não conseguir mais. Ele conta que uma área de vegetação próxima à ocupação foi desmatada recentemente e que, com isso, sentiu mudança na temperatura do entorno. Sobre o futuro empreendimento, Milson se diz preocupado. “Eu costumo dizer que o El Niño já está acontecendo. Hoje eu vejo que estamos com 38 °C. Pode ter certeza que quando começar a funcionar aqui [o datacenter], a gente estará com 40 °C nesse horário.” Toniel Ferreira Barbosa, de 46 anos, também mora na comunidade, mas não tinha noção de que uma empresa de tecnologia se aproximava do seu território. Seu cotidiano é marcado por uma perda recente. O filho morreu há pouco tempo. Entre as hipóteses levantadas pelos médicos estavam asma, pneumonia e tuberculose. Mais tarde, surgiu a suspeita de leptospirose, que foi confirmada por meio de um teste. A doença infecciosa está associada, segundo o Ministério da Saúde, a condições precárias de saneamento básico e a presença de roedores infectados. Mas a confirmação veio tarde demais. “Meu filho foi morrendo aos poucos.” Toniel também precisa de acesso à saúde, mas enfrenta dificuldades para conseguir atendimento. Doente, ele não pode nem deve trabalhar, mas, mesmo assim procura um emprego. Leia também: Sem direitos: como vivem os brasileiros em casas sem banheiro Sobre data centers, seu conhecimento vem sobretudo dos filmes de ação a que assiste, nos quais associa as estruturas a apostas e golpes virtuais. Mesmo sem saber exatamente o que são data centers, ele imagina o que está em risco. “Para quem vive numa calmaria como a gente, na beira do rio, com esse vento que Deus nos dá todos os dias, a nossa vida pode ser transformada num inferno.” Para ele, a possibilidade de uma estrutura desse porte próxima à comunidade é motivo de preocupação concreta caso haja aumento do calor e do barulho durante as 24 horas do dia. Ele resume seu temor: “Se for para botar um data center aqui para destruir a comunidade, tem crianças, muita criança mesmo aqui ao redor. Eu acho que é uma má opção, isso daí a gente tem que botar no local onde não tenha nem vida humana.” O projeto

artigo.texto: EcoPro is stepping up efforts to strengthen its global competitiveness by showcasing its secondary battery materials ecosystem in Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province, and its next-generation battery materials technologies. EcoPro said Sunday that it participated in the International Battery Expo 2026 Pohang, held for three days from Nov. 13 at Manindang Gymnasium in Pohang. Now in its second year, the expo is a specialized exhibition showcasing technologies and future visions across the entire battery industry, from materials and components to recycling used batteries. EcoPro organized its exhibition booth around seven themes, including cooperation with the Pohang community, global supply chains, high-nickel cathode materials and next-generation battery materials. Since 2017, EcoPro has invested approximately 3.3 trillion won in Pohang to build a secondary battery materials ecosystem linking precursor and cathode material production with used battery recycling. The company is strengthening its supply chain competitiveness through a closed-loop system that connects raw material procurement, production and recycling. The company also introduced its global production network. It is building an integrated supply chain linking its BNSI nickel smelter in Indonesia, its cathode materials plant in Debrecen, Hungary, and its domestic production facilities, connecting raw material sourcing with finished product manufacturing. EcoPro also showcased its next-generation battery materials technologies. Its lineup included high-nickel ternary cathode materials, known for their high energy density, as well as mid-nickel cathode materials, materials for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials. The company also presented its solid electrolyte technology, a key material for all-solid-state batteries, outlining its strategy to expand its product portfolio. High-nickel cathode materials, in particular, are expected to find wider applications beyond electric vehicles in emerging industries requiring high energy density, including humanoid robots, urban air mobility (UAM) and aerospace. EcoPro also highlighted its contributions to the local community. Through social initiatives such as supporting childbirth in vulnerable households, providing safety umbrellas for children and developing community welfare villages, the company has been recognized as a community-contributing company for seven consecutive years. "Having grown in Pohang, EcoPro feels a strong responsibility to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of Korea's battery industry alongside the local community," EcoPro CEO Choi Sang-woon said. "We will do our utmost to boost our global competitiveness through continued investment and technological innovation while helping revitalize the local economy and create quality jobs."
