artigo.texto: Botswana battery storage plan puts 100MWh beside the Mmadinare solar cluster Botswana Power Corporation has published plans for a 25MW battery with 100MWh of storage beside the Mmadinare solar cluster, with the World Bank funding its construction, as Botswana presents a climate plan at COP31 in Antalya that ranks energy generation as its largest opportunity for carbon market activity. Botswana Power Corporation has published a revised environmental and social management plan, dated 6 November, for a battery storage system of 25MW and 100MWh in 20 battery containers and five power conversion units, to be built on 2 hectares of a 40-hectare plot 8km south-east of Mmadinare in the Bobirwa District, beside the 100MW Mmadinare Solar PV Cluster. The plan, submitted to the Department of Environmental Protection in Selebi Phikwe, says the World Bank will fund the initial construction, pencilled in for 2027 over 9 to 12 months, and that the battery is designed to firm the output of the adjoining solar cluster and to provide peak-shaving and frequency services for the region. More than 243,288MWh had flowed into the grid from the solar cluster by its official launch on 31 August, with availability and reliability above 99% since operations began, according to BPC’s Chief Executive, David Kgoboko. Scatec, the Norwegian IPP that built and owns the plant, sells its power to BPC under a 25-year power purchase agreement. Solar plants at Bobonong, Phakalane, Shakawe and Mmadinare produced about 82,520MWh in the first quarter of 2026, or 9.1% of domestic generation against 3.2% a year earlier, by Statistics Botswana’s figures reported in Mmegi, while imports fell 29.8% on the previous quarter and the Morupule A and B coal plants supplied 90.8% of local generation. Under its revised Integrated Resource Plan the government wants renewables to supply 50% of the generation mix by 2030, up from about 8%, and in April President Duma Boko broke ground at Maun on a 500MW solar plant with a 500MWh battery, which BPC is executing with Okavango Solar under a government-to-government partnership with Oman and a 30-year power purchase agreement. The World Bank’s Renewable Energy Support and Access Accelerator project, approved in July 2024 with an $88 million loan and $34 million in Green Climate Fund finance, includes 50MW of utility-scale battery storage. Botswana’s third nationally determined contribution, which its delegation is presenting at COP31 in Antalya, rates energy generation as having the “largest” potential for carbon market activities and nature-based removals a “significant” one, with bushfire management and refrigerant transitions at “moderate” and a “lower volume” expected from energy efficiency, according to Argus. Its draft carbon market framework, which Carbon Pulse reported the plan targets for the first quarter of 2027, would keep the cheaper mitigation for Botswana’s own target and offer the higher-cost activities abroad as internationally transferred mitigation outcomes under Article 6, and it names both Article 6.2 and the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism as suitable routes for energy generation. Mitigation under the unconditional target will need $224 million between 2026 and 2035, the NDC says, and the conditional mitigation need for the same period is $1.5 billion. The second NDC, submitted in December 2024, had put the conditional need to 2030 at $2.7 billion, of which about $50 million has been secured, Argus reported. On removals, the NDC cautions against overselling the low-cost mitigation Botswana needs for its own unconditional target, and the government will seek $4.32 billion in climate finance at COP31, the state news agency BOPA reported. Before commissioning, the battery will need grid-connection and regulatory approvals from the Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority, the ESMP says, and amendments to BERA’s own Act that would recognise independent transmission providers and introduce electricity trading are due in Parliament’s November sitting, according to Mmegi’s report of remarks by BERA’s Chief Executive, Never Tshabang, at the National Business Conference in Francistown in October. Fieldwork for the ESMP found no one living on the 40-hectare plot that the Ngwato Land Board allocated to BPC, so no resettlement plan is needed, and the battery compound will fence about 2 hectares, leaving the other 38 open for the livestock of neighbouring farmers and for the communities who collect non-timber forest products there.

artigo.texto: Bangladesh, Singapore sign MoU on carbon market cooperation Speaking at the signing ceremony, Faridul Islam said Bangladesh warmly welcomes the partnership with Singapore under the Paris Agreement. Bangladesh and Singapore have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance cooperation in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, opening up new opportunities for climate financing and joint initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The MoU was signed this morning (14 November) at the Singapore Pavilion on the sidelines of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, said to a press release. State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam signed the agreement on behalf of Bangladesh, while Secretary of Singapore's Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment Melvin Ong signed for his country. The agreement is expected to facilitate Bangladesh's participation in international carbon markets, expand access to carbon financing and environmentally sustainable investments, and support the implementation of the country's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0). Speaking at the signing ceremony, Faridul Islam said Bangladesh warmly welcomes the partnership with Singapore under the Paris Agreement. He said the cooperation would help unlock new opportunities for carbon finance, develop high-quality and transparent carbon markets, and advance the implementation of Bangladesh's NDC 3.0. Bangladesh is committed to working closely with Singapore to promote sustainable development, achieve ambitious climate goals and strengthen effective global climate action, he added. Under the MoU, the two countries will exchange information, knowledge and experience on carbon credits and explore further cooperation in greenhouse gas emission reduction projects based on mutual interests and benefits. The partnership is expected to accelerate climate change mitigation efforts by utilising the opportunities for international cooperation provided under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. It is also expected to support the development of internationally recognised carbon markets in Bangladesh, facilitate the transfer of climate-friendly technologies, attract greater private sector investment and create new avenues for international climate finance. The initiative will further contribute to Bangladesh's transition towards sustainable and low-carbon development and help achieve its national climate targets.

artigo.texto: $100 million license awarded from U.S. Department of Commerce for sale and export of recycled black mass product Major milestone achieved with federal permitting for ABTC's Tonopah Flats Lithium Project, one of the largest identified critical mineral lithium projects in the U.S. Company demonstrates strong cash position along with zero debt RENO, Nev., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- American Battery Technology Company (NASDAQ: ABAT), an integrated domestic critical mineral manufacturing company that is commercializing its internally-developed technologies for both primary critical mineral manufacturing and secondary critical mineral recycling, released the financial results for its first quarter of fiscal year 2027 ended on September 30, 2026. Financial Highlights, First Quarter of FY27: $1.7 million in Revenue, an 83% increase from the same quarter the previous year An additional $0.4 million recorded as interest income for the quarter Substantial increase in finished goods inventory, from the continued commercial scale operations of recycling facility but with the accumulation of product due to temporary federal export ban $5.4 million in Cost of Goods Sold, an only 20% increase from the same quarter the previous year Resulting from implementation of multiple operational efficiencies $43.4 million cash, including $0.1 million in restricted cash $0.0 million debt, Company currently holds zero debt Over the quarter, American Battery Technology Company (ABTC) continued to scale-up and implement operational efficiencies at its Nevada critical mineral recycling facility. While the commercial facility continued operations throughout the quarter, on August 6, 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued a directive in the federal register that it was restricting the export of black mass from recycled battery materials effective August 27, 2026. Recycled black mass is the primary product from ABTC's critical mineral recycling facility, and essentially all of this product is exported for sale. ABTC submitted an exception request for a license to continue to export black mass throughout the approximately one-year duration of this export restriction, and on September 30, 2026, the BIS issued such a license to ABTC. This temporary restriction of the export of black mass resulted in a large accumulation of finished goods inventory within the quarter, and limited sale and recognition of revenue within Q1 FY27. Subsequent to the conclusion of this reporting period, ABTC restarted the large-scale sale and exportation of accumulated black mass product, along with the sale of product made within Q2 to date. "We are excited to have been issued this license and to now be selling the black mass produced within Q1 FY27 along with the black mass we are currently producing and are grateful to our multiple stakeholders and champions who supported us during this process," stated American Battery Technology Company CEO Ryan Melsert. "We are proud of the strong relationships we have built within multiple agencies throughout the U.S. government and across multiple administrations." In addition to operating its critical mineral recycling facility, ABTC is also developing its critical mineral mine and refinery at its Tonopah Flats Lithium Project (TFLP) near Tonopah, Nevada. During the quarter ABTC announced that it has received acceptance of its Plan of Operations by the U.S. BLM for the construction and operations of its TFLP, which is a major milestone in the commercialization of one of the largest identified critical mineral lithium resources in the United States. artigo.texto: The Greek Ministry of Environment and Energy has released its long-awaited list of merchant battery storage projects, totaling 4.7 GW. Earlier this year, the first battery energy storage systems were put into operation, from the 900 MW in operating power that received government support through auctions. The next step is to install the 4.7 GW with no support – operating purely under market conditions. The ministry said it received 831 applications for 12,319 MW. Out of these, 221 or 10,521 MW were for the transmission network and 610 or 1,798 MW for the distribution system. After evaluation, projects of 6,366 MW altogether were selected as either frontrunners or substitutes in the first case, and 1,403 MW in the latter. All in all, 4,700 MW would receive connection terms. Which companies succeeded Among the protagonists in the large segment, Public Power Corporation (PPC) secured five projects for a total capacity of 470 MW, with all but one located in coal regions, including the Florina area in the north. HELLENiQ Renewables, the green branch of Greek refiner HELLENiQ Energy, passed with 50 MW. Other well-known names in the renewables sector in the catalogue are Masdar’s Terna Energy with 197.5 MW, Rokas with 220 MW, Lightsource with 80 MW, Aenaos with 198 MW and ABO with 95 MW, all to be connected to the transmission grid. Hundreds of investments by smaller companies are on the list for the Hellenic Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO or DEDDIE). Mid-term goal set at up to 7 GW According to the government, the ultimate goal is to have 5 GW to 7 GW of storage capacity in operation by 2028. It would reduce forced curtailments of renewable energy production and raise wholesale prices during the day, helping the struggling solar power producers. Batteries are expected to reduce the overall energy costs for consumers, too. As for the next steps, the two network operators will have to provide connection terms. This will occur in phases, based on connection priority for each project category.

artigo.texto: As ações da Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) caem 2,7% nas negociações pré-mercado de sexta-feira, ampliando as perdas da sessão anterior, enquanto os investidores avaliavam os resultados financeiros do terceiro trimestre da empresa, as expectativas de receita revisadas e as previsões de despesas de capital aumentadas. A queda ocorreu após o anúncio dos resultados da Nebius em 12 de novembro, que reportou um crescimento substancial da receita em relação ao ano anterior, mas também delineou atrasos na capacidade planejada de data centers e maiores necessidades de investimento para 2026 e 2027. A atualização das orientações da empresa levou os analistas a reduzirem suas metas de preço das ações, enquanto a incerteza generalizada em torno das empresas de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial aumentou a pressão do mercado. O que a Nebius divulgou em seus resultados do terceiro trimestre? A Nebius reportou uma receita de US$ 980,8 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, representando um aumento de 571% em comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior. O valor superou as expectativas consensuais dos analistas, refletindo o crescimento das operações de infraestrutura de IA da empresa. No entanto, a Nebius também indicou que sua receita para o ano de 2026 agora deverá ficar na extremidade inferior da faixa de projeção anteriormente anunciada, de US$ 3 bilhões a US$ 3,4 bilhões. A empresa atribuiu a mudança a atrasos na obtenção de capacidade de data center de terceiros para colocation, o que afetou o cronograma de geração de receita planejado. A receita associada à capacidade adiada deverá agora ser reconhecida durante o primeiro semestre de 2027. A revisão das perspectivas refletiu, portanto, uma mudança no cronograma esperado de receita, e não uma redução nas vendas reportadas pela empresa no terceiro trimestre. Por que a Nebius aumentou sua previsão de gastos de capital? A Nebius elevou sua previsão de despesas de capital para 2026 para aproximadamente US$ 27 bilhões, em comparação com a previsão anterior, que variava de US$ 20 bilhões a US$ 25 bilhões. A empresa também apresentou expectativas preliminares de investimento de capital entre US$ 40 bilhões e US$ 45 bilhões para 2027. A previsão de gastos para o próximo ano superou as estimativas anteriores dos analistas, aumentando a atenção sobre a escala de investimento necessária para expandir a capacidade da infraestrutura de IA da Nebius. Os investimentos de capital continuam sendo um fator importante para os investidores que avaliam as necessidades futuras de caixa da empresa e os retornos potenciais de seu programa de desenvolvimento de infraestrutura. A Nebius afirmou que os pagamentos antecipados de clientes relacionados a contratos assinados durante o terceiro trimestre cobriram mais de 100% do investimento de capital vinculado a esses contratos. A empresa também delineou as expectativas para seu desempenho financeiro à medida que a capacidade de infraestrutura adicional entrar em operação. O diretor executivo, Arkady Volozh, indicou que a Nebius tinha como meta atingir o ponto de equilíbrio antes dos impostos até o final de 2027. Apesar dessas declarações, o aumento das previsões de investimento levou os investidores a reavaliarem a relação entre as despesas planejadas, a geração de receita e o momento da potencial rentabilidade. Como os analistas reagiram às novas orientações da Nebius? Após o anúncio dos resultados financeiros, diversas empresas de investimento revisaram suas metas de preço para as ações da Nebius. A Baird reduziu seu preço-alvo de US$ 340 para US$ 200, enquanto a Piper Sandler diminuiu o seu de US$ 185 para US$ 148. Apesar das reduções, ambas as empresas mantiveram suas classificações de ações existentes. As metas revisadas refletiram a reavaliação das perspectivas financeiras da empresa pelos analistas, após as mudanças no cronograma de receita e nas expectativas de despesas de capital. Os ajustes aumentaram a atenção do mercado em torno da capacidade da Nebius de executar seus planos de expansão de infraestrutura, gerenciando simultaneamente as necessidades financeiras associadas ao seu programa de investimentos. O mercado mais amplo de infraestrutura de IA está afetando as ações da Nebius? A movimentação do preço das ações da Nebius também ocorreu durante um período de incerteza em todo o setor de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. O índice Nasdaq Composite caiu aproximadamente 0,2% na sexta-feira, enquanto diversas empresas associadas à infraestrutura de IA continuaram a enfrentar pressão vendedora. O setor foi afetado pelos acontecimentos na Nvidia após a saída do CEO Jensen Huang, o que levou os investidores a reavaliarem a liderança e a incerteza estratégica em uma das principais fornecedoras de hardware de computação de IA. As ações de outras empresas de infraestrutura de IA, incluindo a CoreWeave, também foram afetadas pela reação mais ampla do mercado em 12 de novembro. Esses desenvolvimentos coincidiram com o escrutínio contínuo dos investidores em relação ao montante de capital destinado a centros de dados, equipamentos de informática e infraestrutura relacionada. Para a Nebius, o contexto setorial reforçou a avaliação do mercado em relação às previsões financeiras e aos compromissos de investimento da própria empresa. O que os investidores estão observando a seguir em relação à Nebius? Após a última queda, as ações da Nebius estavam sendo negociadas abaixo de sua máxima de 52 semanas, de US$ 299,86. Os resultados do terceiro trimestre da empresa demonstraram um aumento substancial na receita reportada, enquanto suas projeções atualizadas destacaram as diferenças de cronograma entre o investimento em infraestrutura e o reconhecimento da receita associada. Os investidores estão agora monitorando se a capacidade de colocation de terceiros, que estava atrasada, estará disponível conforme o esperado durante o primeiro semestre de 2027. artigo.texto: A Patagônia entrou na disputa por grandes estruturas de inteligência artificial, mas o tamanho da promessa ainda supera o estágio dos projetos. Na Argentina, a Green Capital propõe um data center de US$ 3 bilhões em Chubut, enquanto o governo busca atrair investidores com flexibilização e incentivos. A iniciativa expõe uma questão territorial: computação exige terra, energia e água, mesmo quando seus serviços circulam pela internet. Entre no canal do WhatsApp da Geocracia O projeto envolve uma área de 130 mil hectares e negociações com catorze proprietários. A construção não começaria antes de 2028, e ainda há licenças, estudos e contratação de clientes a resolver. A combinação energética prevista inclui fontes eólica, solar e gás. Esses elementos descrevem uma proposta em preparação, não um empreendimento já instalado ou um investimento integralmente confirmado e executado. A dimensão da demanda energética e a falta de definição pública sobre o consumo de água alimentam questionamentos locais. Em Trelew, moradores e organizações pedem informações sobre o uso dos recursos e os efeitos do empreendimento. Para avaliar o projeto, interessa saber como será abastecido, quais contrapartidas haverá e de que maneira os impactos serão distribuídos entre investidores, população e atividades já existentes. A reportagem da Associated Press descreve outras iniciativas, como planos da Pampa Energía associados ao gás de Vaca Muerta, e registra que investidores aguardam maior clareza sobre as condições políticas e regulatórias. Também apresenta dúvidas sobre o benefício local de estruturas voltadas à exportação de capacidade computacional. A atração de servidores, por si só, não esclarece quais empregos, serviços e receitas permaneceriam nas regiões escolhidas. A IA pode cometer erros. Consulte as fontes e a matéria original. Já conversou com o território hoje? Experimente a Geocracia.ai No Olhar Digital, Valdir Antonelli relata a proposta de redução tributária para grandes projetos e informa que ela ainda depende de tramitação legislativa. O texto se baseia na apuração da AP. O quadro deve ser lido como disputa por uma infraestrutura futura: incentivos anunciados, investimento projetado e instalações operacionais são estágios distintos, e a viabilidade territorial permanece parte central da decisão. Apuração complementar: Reportagem da Associated Press ISSN 3086-0415, edição de Luiz Ugeda.

artigo.texto: MARS Energy Group Adds Jigar Shah to Advisory Board to Accelerate Battery Storage Growth SunEdison founder and former U.S. Department of Energy loan chief joins as battery storage becomes central to MARS's growth. SACRAMENTO, Calif., November 13, 2026 (Newswire.com) - MARS Energy Group (MARS), a national solar, roofing, and energy storage company, today announced that Jigar Shah has joined its Advisory Board. Shah, one of the most influential entrepreneurs and investors in clean energy, will advise MARS as it builds dedicated battery divisions within each of its operating companies and makes storage a growing part of its business. Shah, named to the 2024 TIME100 list of the world's most influential people, is an energy entrepreneur and strategist focused on scaling the infrastructure needed for the clean energy transition. Most recently, Shah served as Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's Loan Programs Office, expanding its authority tenfold and helping deploy more than $100 billion into domestic manufacturing, advanced transportation, and energy infrastructure. He founded SunEdison, where he pioneered the third-party solar power purchase agreement model that helped launch the global solar industry, and later co-founded Generate Capital, advancing the infrastructure-as-a-service model. Shah brings a pragmatic, execution-focused perspective to the energy transition, emphasizing the ability to build at speed and scale as a central challenge. "Batteries are becoming central to everything we do, from new homes and existing homeowners to commercial projects," said Manvendra Saxena, Chairman and CEO of MARS Energy Group. "We're not asking our solar teams to do batteries on the side. We're building a dedicated battery division within each of our companies, with the focus and talent it deserves. There is no one better than Jigar to help us do it at scale." MARS installs solar, battery storage, and roofing for homebuilders, homeowners, and commercial and public-sector customers, with more than 1,600 employees across 14 offices nationwide. That footprint provides an established foundation for storage growth: new homes, existing solar customers ready to add batteries, and commercial sites that need reliable, flexible power. "Storage is where the next decade of value in distributed energy will be created, and the winners will be the companies that can install and service it at scale," said Shah. "MARS already has the crews, the customer relationships, and the builder partnerships. Building dedicated battery divisions across that platform is the right move, and I'm excited to help the team do it." About MARS Energy Group MARS Energy Group is a national energy infrastructure company delivering solar, battery energy storage, and roofing solutions for homebuilders, homeowners, businesses, and public agencies. With more than 1,600 employees across 14 offices nationwide, MARS provides integrated engineering, procurement, construction, and long-term service through its specialized operating companies. Contact: Cody Kilmer Chief Experience Officer cody@marsenergygroup.com SOURCE: Mars Energy Group Source: Mars Energy Group

artigo.texto: CATL is exploring an air-breathing battery. Could it give EVs 2,000 km of range? A report by Chinese technology outlet IT Home has revived claims that lithium-air batteries could deliver electric vehicle ranges of up to 2,000 km and achieve five times the energy density of solid-state batteries. The chemistry’s theoretical specific energy is often cited at around 3,505 Wh/kg. However, this figure describes electrochemical potential, not the performance of a complete automotive battery. The CATL connection comes from Chief Scientist Wu Kai, who identified lithium-air technology as a long-term research direction at the 2026 Equipment Powerhouse Forum. As we previously reported, CATL’s broader battery roadmap places sodium-ion and all-solid-state technologies closer to commercialisation, while lithium-air remains a longer-term research prospect. CATL has not announced a 2,000 km production-car target or a commercial launch schedule for the technology. The gap between theoretical energy density and automotive performance remains substantial. Oxygen management, chemical stability, rechargeability and the supporting equipment all present significant engineering challenges. How lithium-air batteries work Conventional lithium-ion batteries store lithium within two electrodes, with lithium ions moving between the anode and cathode during charging and discharging. Lithium-air batteries instead use metallic lithium as the negative electrode and oxygen from the surrounding environment as the positive reactant. During discharge, lithium reacts with oxygen to form lithium peroxide (Li₂O₂) inside a porous cathode. Charging reverses the reaction, releasing oxygen and returning lithium ions to the anode. Drawing oxygen from outside the cell rather than storing the positive reactant in a conventional cathode material gives the chemistry high theoretical specific energy. The frequently cited 3,505 Wh/kg figure relates to the theoretical lithium-peroxide reaction and includes the oxygen reactant mass. Higher figures approaching 12,000 Wh/kg use a different calculation boundary that excludes oxygen mass. Neither represents the energy density of a complete automotive battery. Electrolytes, electrodes, protective components and air-management equipment all add weight and volume. Laboratory progress has not solved the durability problem Automotive interest in lithium-air batteries predates CATL’s research. IBM launched its Battery 500 project in 2009, targeting a metal-air battery capable of powering an electric car for 500 miles (805 km) on a charge. The multinational research programme involved academic and industry partners but did not produce a commercially available automotive battery. More recent research has addressed lithium-air batteries’ chemical limitations, particularly the accumulation of discharge products inside porous cathodes. A 2025 study by researchers at the University of Science and Technology of China, including Professor Peng Tan, examined how electrolyte oxygen-transport properties influence reaction mechanisms in lithium-oxygen batteries. Using thick electrodes, the researchers showed how mass-transfer resistance can change reaction pathways at different positions within an electrode. The work provides insight into electrode design but does not establish an automotive solution to cathode blockage. A separate result came from researchers associated with Jilin University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences. A 2024 study published in Advanced Energy Materials reported an optimised lithium-air pouch-cell configuration achieving 757.5 Wh/kg with an in-situ gelled polymer electrolyte. The researchers also demonstrated 241 cycles under specified laboratory conditions of 500 mA/g and 1,000 mAh/g. This is a laboratory result, not a commercially validated automotive battery-pack rating. Researchers at the Illinois Institute of Technology and Argonne National Laboratory reported another approach in a 2023 Science paper. Their solid-state lithium-air architecture used a four-electron reaction to form lithium oxide (Li₂O), rather than the more conventional lithium-peroxide pathway. The battery completed at least 1,000 charge-discharge cycles at room temperature. Its theoretical energy-density potential was estimated at 1,200 Wh/kg, not measured as an achieved commercial-cell rating. These results show progress beyond theoretical calculations, but different chemistries, operating environments and measurement boundaries make direct comparisons difficult. None establishes a production-ready passenger-car battery. Three engineering roadblocks for passenger cars 1. Air management adds weight and complexity A lithium-air battery needs oxygen while limiting exposure to moisture and carbon dioxide. These contaminants can trigger unwanted reactions that degrade the lithium anode, electrolyte and cathode. Moisture can react with metallic lithium, while carbon dioxide can form lithium carbonate (Li₂CO₃). Deposits inside the porous cathode can restrict oxygen transport and reduce usable capacity. An automotive system would therefore need controlled air intake, filtration and humidity management, potentially alongside additional gas-handling equipment. These components add weight and volume while consuming energy. A 2023 study in the Journal of Energy Storage proposed mechanical balance-of-plant systems for lithium-air vehicles. It estimated that the supporting equipment would consume 5.4% of battery power in its proposed vehicle configuration. The figure is design-specific, but illustrates the additional energy demand of operating lithium-air cells in a vehicle. 2. Rechargeability and efficiency remain difficult Lithium peroxide must be removed from the cathode during charging. Reversing the discharge reaction requires additional energy and can generate reactive oxygen species that attack the electrolyte and other cell components. artigo.texto: A empresa que instalaria o primeiro data center de grande escala de Pernambuco, voltado para mineração de criptomoedas, desistiu do investimento. O empreendimento chamado Engedata, pertencente a Eólica Serra das Vacas, já tinha licença de instalação emitida pela Agência Estadual de Meio Ambiente (CPRH) — mesmo não tendo consultado as comunidades rurais locais. Ele seria construído no município de Paranatama, no agreste, a 250 quilômetros do Recife, onde a companhia já opera um parque eólico de mesmo nome há mais de 10 anos. O anúncio da desistência foi feito pela CPRH em audiência pública convocada pelo Ministério Público de Pernambuco (MPPE), na quarta-feira, 11 de novembro, em Garanhuns. O evento aconteceu para debater os impactos hídricos, energéticos e socioambientais desse tipo de empreendimento no estado, pois se trata de infraestruturas de alto consumo de energia e de água, que causam um barulho ensurdecedor, demandam minérios, produzem lixo eletrônico e prejudicam a vida nos territórios. A audiência teve um foco especial na situação de Paranatama, onde famílias agricultoras já sofrem as consequências da presença de turbinas eólicas e poderiam ser revitimizadas por um data center. A atual sobreoferta de energia eólica atrai as grandes estruturas de computadores, ávidas por água e energia, transformando, mais uma vez, o semiárido nordestino, uma região de escassez hídrica, em “zona de sacrifício”, dizem especialistas e ambientalistas críticos a esses negócios. Na audiência, Danuza Ferraz, da diretoria de licenciamento da CPRH, informou que a licença para instalação da Engedata foi emitida em maio deste ano. Em junho, o Conselho Nacional do Meio Ambiente (Conama) aprovou a Moção nº 147/2026, que estabelece diretrizes para endurecer e padronizar o licenciamento ambiental de data centers no Brasil, com foco especial nas estruturas voltadas à inteligência artificial. “Também foi recomendada aos órgãos licenciadores a suspensão e revisão de licenças até o estabelecimento de diretrizes e parâmetros. A CPRH conversou com a empresa para dizer que iria fazer essa suspensão porque foi verificado que estudos a mais deveriam ser solicitados. A empresa comunicou que não teria mais interesse no empreendimento”, relatou a representante da agência. A solicitação de cancelamento, segundo ela, foi protocolada na CPRH na terça (10). A Marco Zero não conseguiu contato com a Eólica Serra das Vacas. Representando a Secretaria de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação de Pernambuco (Secti), Noemi Resende anunciou, durante a audiência, que a pasta contratou um estudo sobre data centers. O estudo, porém, envolve apenas empresas privadas, pois foi encomendado à consultoria Deloitte em parceria com o Lide PE, uma aliança que reúne lideranças empresariais e o Governo do Estado. Na semana passada, diversas organizações, entre elas o Greenpeace e o Instituto Terramar, ocuparam as ruas de Fortaleza (CE), Belém (PA) e Pindamonhangaba (SP) para dizer “não” à expansão desenfreada dos mega data centers. As três cidades possuem projetos em andamento. As mobilizações se somaram a atos internacionais que também alertam para os impactos desses empreendimentos. Uma onda de protestos coordenados em pelo menos 15 países europeus pediu a suspensão dessas construções. Manifestantes chegaram a invadir o canteiro de obras da Microsoft em Amsterdã, na Holanda. Nos Estados Unidos, uma pesquisa da emissora de TV NBC News com eleitores na boca da urna da eleição de meio mandato, no início do mês, apontou que 57% acreditam que a IA fará mais mal que bem à sociedade e que 76% eram contrários a essas construções em suas comunidades. Há basicamente dois tipos de data centers. Os chamados edge (de borda) são instalações pequenas, espalhadas e próximas dos usuários, muitas vezes dentro de prédios nas cidades. Servem para reduzir o tempo de resposta da internet (a latência), em aplicações como streaming, internet das coisas ou cirurgia remota. Os que vêm causando problemas mais sérios são os de hiperescala. São complexos gigantescos, com galpões que podem ocupar áreas equivalentes a dezenas de campos de futebol e consumir centenas de megawatts. Concentram enorme capacidade de processamento para nuvem e inteligência artificial e, por isso, exigem energia dedicada e muita refrigeração. Em Pernambuco, há três em funcionamento, todos no Recife e do tipo edge. Saiba mais sobre os impactos em reportagem da MZ. “O que estamos discutindo aqui é que existia uma licença de instalação sem que nenhum morador da comunidade tenha sido consultado”, chamou a atenção, durante a audiência pública, o advogado da Comissão Pastoral da Terra (CPT) João Victor Venâncio. “Estamos aqui para, primeiro de tudo, demarcar a irresponsabilidade da Agência Estadual de Meio Ambiente”, denunciou, após comemorar como uma “vitória popular” que a Eólica Serra das Vacas tenha desistido da Engedata. “Os documentos a que tivemos acesso tinham basicamente o memorial descritivo do empreendimento. Não tinham sequer um estudo de impacto ambiental. Portanto, quais seriam os impactos dessa penca de computadores, de servidores, de máquinas que seriam instaladas ali para ficar minerando bitcoin, minerando dinheiro para quem já tem dinheiro?”, disparou. “Eles prometem que isso é desenvolvimento econômico. Quem é da região sabe que eles também prometeram isso com as eólicas e os complexos solares. Mas algum morador aqui de Caetés, Venturosa ou Paranatama está empregado nesses complexos? Não, não é? Estamos falando de pessoas que estão há 10 anos sem dormir (por causa do barulho das torres eólicas)”, provocou o advogado, para mostrar que empreendimentos de energia não costumam gerar emprego e renda para as comunidades locais em sua fase de operação. artigo.texto: QNA DOHA The Global Carbon Council (GCC) and Turkiye’s Energy Exchange, Enerji Piyasaları İşletme AŞ (EPİAŞ), internationally known as Energy Exchange Istanbul (EXIST), have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation on carbon market development and explore opportunities for trading GCC-issued carbon credits in Türkiye. The agreement was signed at the Arab Climate Pavilion jointly hosted by GCC and the League of Arab States during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, by Dr Yousef Alhorr, Founding Chairman of GCC, and Taha Meli Arvas, CEO and Vice Chairman of the Board of EPİAŞ. The cooperation aims to facilitate the use of GCC’s internationally recognized carbon crediting program in Türkiye, explore new opportunities for market participants to access high-integrity carbon credits, and strengthen technical capacity as the country develops its carbon market framework. The agreement brings together GCC’s experience in carbon crediting standards, project registration and credit issuance with EPİAŞ’s expertise in operating organized energy and environmental markets. It seeks to support the development of transparent market mechanisms that can connect credible emissions reduction projects with buyers and investors, while contributing to corporate climate strategies and national climate objectives. Under the MoU, both organizations will explore the listing and trading of GCC’s Approved Carbon Credits (ACCs) on EPİAŞ’s trading platforms, subject to applicable regulations and market requirements. They will also examine the potential recognition of ACCs under Türkiye’s future compliance carbon market framework. The proposed cooperation could broaden market access for project developers and buyers, while encouraging the registration, issuance and use of high-quality carbon credits through transparent and reliable trading processes. Beyond trading, the agreement places strong emphasis on capacity building and knowledge exchange. GCC and EPİAŞ intend to organize workshops, webinars, seminars and other activities to strengthen understanding of carbon market requirements among potential market participants and local stakeholders. GCC will also support access to publicly available information on its crediting program, registry and methodologies. The cooperation may further draw on the expertise of the Gulf Organisation for Research and Development (GORD), GCC’s parent organization, to support market readiness and technical capacity development in Türkiye. Potential areas of support include training on greenhouse gas accounting, monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV), carbon border adjustment requirements, and sustainability disclosure under the Turkish Sustainability Reporting Standards (TSRS), which are aligned with IFRS S1 and S2. The parties may also explore the application of GORD’s digital solutions, including SustainoAI, to support greenhouse gas accounting, ESG reporting and financed-emissions calculations, alongside broader technical assistance in decarbonization and energy efficiency. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Yousef Alhorr, Founding Chairman of the Global Carbon Council, said: “Credible carbon markets depend on the ability to connect high-integrity carbon credits with transparent, well-functioning market infrastructure. Our cooperation with EPİAŞ creates an opportunity to strengthen these connections in Türkiye while supporting the knowledge and institutional capacity needed for markets to grow responsibly. Beyond trading, the broader objective is to help climate projects attract investment, deliver measurable emissions reductions and contribute to sustainable economic development.” The agreement reflects a shared interest in strengthening Türkiye’s carbon market ecosystem through internationally recognized standards, technical cooperation and the exchange of expertise. By bringing together carbon crediting and organized market operations, GCC and EPİAŞ aim to support the development of credible and accessible market mechanisms that can translate climate commitments into measurable outcomes. Commenting on the agreement, Taha Meli Arvas, CEO and Vice Chairman of the Board of EPİAŞ, said: “Developing effective carbon markets requires more than trading platforms. It depends on reliable standards, transparent processes and participants who have the knowledge and capacity to engage with confidence. Through our cooperation with the Global Carbon Council, we aim to explore new opportunities for carbon credit trading, strengthen technical expertise and support market development in line with Türkiye’s regulatory priorities and evolving market needs.”

artigo.texto: By Staff Reporter | Arizona’s Democratic executive and legislative leadership have proposed that their first priority for 2027 would be a data center moratorium. Newly reelected Attorney General Kris Mayes, along with Senate President-elect Priya Sundareshan (D-LD18), have stated that the first focus for Democrats come January should be to stop data center development. Mayes said on election night that she supports a moratorium, and Sundareshan agreed. Sundareshan told The Center Square that a moratorium would be the first step to take while their party determines what water and energy requirements for data centers look like. “I think there’s a lot more that needs to be done that we are talking [about], that would make sure that data centers are addressing their water and energy use and being good neighbors in the process,” said Sundareshan. “So, the data center moratorium that Attorney General Mayes has proposed until we can figure out those requirements may well be one way to go.” Gov. Katie Hobbs has been more reluctant about an outright moratorium, opting instead for measures that indirectly check growth by requiring data centers to pay their own way when it comes to taxes and charges for using resources. Sundareshan claimed in a celebration rally remark on Tuesday at the state capitol that Hobbs was likely to change her mind now that Democrats have secured a historic trifecta and triplex. “Some of those conversations were before we entered this new day in Arizona,” said Sundareshan. “I think what we need to see is what we can do to be responsive to the voters at the same time as recognizing that there are some benefits that the industry might bring.” On Thursday, however, Hobbs issued an indirect response to Sundareshan’s claim by telling 12News that she wants more requirements for data centers, not a complete halt on development. Hobbs proposed requiring data centers to address the concerns of the neighborhoods they come into and to absorb the costs of their operations, specifically concerning water and electricity usage. “My top priority when it comes to data centers is making sure they are working for Arizonans, and not the other way around,” said Hobbs. “We have to make sure that data centers are paying for themselves, that they’re not shifting energy costs on to other ratepayers, that they are using water sustainably.” Arizona has already limited incentives for data centers. The state enacted a tax exemption moratorium on data centers as part of its budget earlier this year, set to expire in 2029. Christian Slater, Hobbs’ communications director, told The Center Square that there are talks to make that moratorium permanent. Senate minority leader-elect John Kavanagh (R-LD3) said it was too late for Democrats to stop the data centers with the moratorium, arguing that it has proven ineffective to stop data center development. “It’ll probably make no difference because the governor’s ordered moratorium was so poorly worded that they have over 100 data centers already in the pipeline that they can’t stop,” said Kavanagh. “I think it’s a real mistake to declare a moratorium on them because we really need them, not only for defense but just for the computing services and amenities that we all rely on every day.” AZ Free News is your #1 source for Arizona news and politics. artigo.texto: Data centers podem atrair R$ 1 trilhão em investimentos ao Brasil até 2036 | Vero NotíciasData centers podem atrair R$ 1 trilhão em investimentos ao Brasil até 2036 O Brasil poderá receber até R$ 1 trilhão em investimentos em data centers até 2036, segundo estimativa da Associação Brasileira de Data Center (ABDC). O crescimento é impulsionado pela inteligência artificial, por incentivos fiscais e pela oferta de energia renovável. A Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) projeta que o setor responderá por cerca de 3% do consumo nacional de eletricidade em 2036, aumentando a necessidade de fontes capazes de garantir fornecimento contínuo. Especialistas apontam que a expansão poderá estimular investimentos em termelétricas a gás natural, além de exigir melhorias nas redes de transmissão e em sistemas de armazenamento de energia. Dados da O Globo. O secretário de Comércio dos Estados Unidos, Howard Lutnick, enfrenta críticas de integrantes do governo Trump por sua relação com Jensen Huang, ex-CEO da Nvidia, e pela demora em restringir exportações de chips avançados à China. Autoridades questionam a decisão de não incluir a empresa Megaspeed, suspeita de repassar tecnologia americana ao mercado chinês, em uma lista de restrições comerciais. Os Correios registraram prejuízo de R$ 1,9 bilhão no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 19% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. Entre janeiro e setembro, as perdas acumuladas chegaram a R$ 7,48 bilhões, crescimento de 27%. A estatal atribui parte das dificuldades à queda nas receitas com encomendas e entregas internacionais, além do aumento de despesas judiciais e financeiras. Cinco economistas avaliam que o ajuste fiscal do governo Lula, voltado a alcançar superávit de 0,5% do PIB em 2027, é insuficiente para conter o crescimento da dívida pública, próxima de 83% do PIB. Entre as propostas estão mudanças na correção do salário mínimo, revisão dos pisos de gastos com saúde e educação e maior controle das despesas obrigatórias. As medidas buscam estabilizar a dívida e abrir espaço para a redução dos juros. O presidente do Federal Reserve de Kansas City, Jeff Schmid, afirmou neste domingo (15) que a inflação nos Estados Unidos permanece acima da meta de 2% e apresenta uma trajetória preocupante. Durante uma conferência no Havaí, Schmid destacou que o banco central possui instrumentos para controlar a alta dos preços, mas não defendeu explicitamente novos aumentos dos juros. As regras de transição da aposentadoria pelo INSS serão atualizadas em janeiro de 2027, conforme a Reforma da Previdência de 2019. As mudanças atingem trabalhadores CLT, autônomos, PJs e MEIs que já contribuíam antes da reforma. A idade mínima progressiva passará a ser de 60 anos para mulheres e 65 para homens, com exigência de 30 e 35 anos de contribuição, respectivamente. Na regra dos pontos, serão necessários 94 pontos para mulheres e 104 para homens.

artigo.texto: The Auburndale City Commission meets Monday night with church zoning and fence setbacks on its agenda. The data center planned for Pace Road is not on it. Residents will likely bring it up during public comment anyway. Roughly 500 people packed a workshop on the project Tuesday, Tampa Bay 28’s Chad Millsreports. City Manager Jeffrey Brown says the Commission does not need to vote again because zoning approved in 2023 already allows a data center. Data centers were an issue in the Governor’s race, too. Gov.-elect Byron Donaldscampaigned on local control against David Jolly, who wanted a moratorium. Donalds said Tuesday that a community that says no does not get a data center. I started FloridAI in May and have spent much of this year tracking the data center fight and the Flock camera fight in St. Petersburg. I don’t pretend to be an expert on either technology. I do understand the politics, and the politics treat every data center as the same data center. Some projects deserve the fight they get, but this one is not the boogeyman. The developer, Texas-based Hillwood, lays out its numbers in an FAQ on the project’s website. The project would convert two existing warehouses on 75 acres already zoned industrial, so no land gets cleared. Hillwood says it is about a tenth the size of a hyperscale data center. It would still draw a lot of power, 350 megawatts in the first phase and 700 at full build-out. Hillwood says it will pay 100% of the cost to generate and deliver that power, which SB 484now requires. Tampa Electric’s proposed tariff would lock that into a contract of at least 20 years. Cooling runs on a closed loop that recirculates the same fluid, which keeps daily water use at about 4,665 gallons by Hillwood’s count. It says a warehouse the same size would use about 10,000 and a golf course about 100,000. The earlier plan for these buildings was distribution. Hillwood says a data center takes 267 semi-truck trips a day off the road. Sound walls are planned, and Hillwood expects noise near what the neighborhood hears now. Hillwood projects about 292 permanent jobs averaging $80,000 a year and more than $1 billion in tax revenue to the city over 15 years. It says that money could pay for new fire stations and water and wastewater improvements. Several of those claims still have to clear regulators. Swiftmud’s Governing Board has to approve a change to the site’s water permit. The Public Service Commission has not yet ruled on Tampa Electric’s tariff. City staff are still reviewing the building permit Hillwood filed Nov. 4. Oh, and one more thing. Former gubernatorial candidate James Fishback wrote to Donalds on Thursday asking him to stop the project. Whatever side Fishback takes, the opposite one is usually the better bet.

artigo.texto: The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) received twenty-two bids from prospective companies to develop 10 GWh of Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) battery manufacturing capacity in India. The initiative aims to expand domestic battery production, particularly for grid-scale energy storage applications. Capacity Targeted for Grid-Scale Energy Storage The government has earmarked the ten GWh manufacturing capacity for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage (GSSS) applications under the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage. The programme aims to establish a total domestic ACC battery manufacturing capacity of 50 GWh, supporting India’s growing energy storage requirements. Technical Bids Opened in November 2026 MHI floated the global tender on the Central Public Procurement Portal on 15 July 2026 and subsequently conducted a pre-bid conference on 29 July 2026. Following the bidding process, the ministry opened the technical bids on 11 November 2026. Participating companies include ACME Solar Holdings, Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, Avaada Electro, Exide Energy Solutions, Fujiyama Power Systems, Vikram Solar and Waaree Energy Storage Solutions, among others. PLI Scheme to Strengthen Domestic Battery Manufacturing Approved in May 2021 with a budgetary allocation of ₹18,100 crore, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme aims to strengthen India’s domestic ACC battery manufacturing ecosystem. The scheme seeks to attract global investments, encourage advanced battery technology development and establish a competitive domestic supply chain for energy storage solutions. As reported by projectstoday.ai, through this initiative, the government aims to reduce import dependence while supporting India’s expanding electric mobility and renewable energy sectors.

artigo.texto: The Greek government’s latest legislation covering the electricity market and the installation of data centers has come into force. It aims to alleviate public mistrust toward these installations, through reciprocal benefits. The new law sets specific requirements when it comes to data centers’ connection to the grid and the use of energy. Specifically, at least 60% of power must originate from renewable energy sources. As a last-minute addition to the law, electricity from outside the country can also cover the needs of data centers. This is important for projects such as the Greece-Egypt electricity interconnection, GREGY, which is currently in its planning stage. Communities to receive annual payments Data centers will have to pay EUR 20,000 per MW annually to local communities, with municipalities receiving 75% and individual consumers 25%. It is the same recipe as for renewable energy installations. Another improvement concerns the letters of guarantee submitted by investors to the authorities. If a data center is only partially built, the owner will not lose the entire sum, but only a proportionate amount of that money. Applications now at 11 GW According to sources from the sector, interest in investing in data centers in Greece currently amounts to about EUR 10 billion. In energy terms, Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO or ADMIE) and Hellenic Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO or DEDDIE) have received applications reaching a total of 11 GW, up from 5 GW earlier this year. IPTO: Three challenges for data center development Recently, Vice Chairman of IPTO Ioannis Margaris said there are three main challenges regarding data center development in the country: energy adequacy, network congestion and power prices for consumers. “There is talk about flexible data centers, which increase or decrease their demand based on conditions in the market. It is similar to licensing flexible renewable energy plants”, he noted.

artigo.texto: Justiça dá 15 dias para Volvo divulgar plano de troca das baterias do EX30 Decisão obriga Volvo a detalhar a substituição da bateria do EX30 sob pena de multa; marca afirma que campanha já está em andamento A Volvo Car Brasil terá de apresentar um cronograma atualizado para a substituição dos módulos de bateria de unidades do EX30 incluídas em uma campanha de recall. A determinação foi proferida em 6 de novembro de 2026 pela Justiça do Rio de Janeiro, em ação civil pública movida pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Defesa dos Direitos dos Consumidores (Abracont). A decisão estabelece prazo de 15 dias (contados desde 6 de novembro) para que a fabricante informe as etapas do procedimento, a disponibilidade de peças, as previsões de atendimento e os critérios de prioridade. A empresa também deverá comunicar individualmente os proprietários afetados, indicando a situação de cada veículo, sua posição no cronograma e as orientações de segurança. O processo tramita na 3ª Vara Empresarial do Rio de Janeiro, mas a juíza Maria Izabel Gomes Santanna de Araujo, da 6ª Vara Empresarial atendeu parcialmente os pedidos feitos pela entidade contra a Volvo. A decisão prevê multa diária de R$ 10 mil em caso de descumprimento injustificado das determinações, limitada inicialmente a R$ 300 mil. A magistrada, porém, não concedeu todos os pedidos apresentados pelo instituto. O fornecimento de carro reserva aos consumidores e o pagamento de compensação financeira mensal foram negados neste primeiro momento. A análise dessas solicitações ficará a cargo da 6ª Vara Empresarial. O Ministério Público havia recomendado justamente o deferimento parcial da tutela, concentrado na apresentação do cronograma e na comunicação aos clientes. Na avaliação da juíza, a limitação preventiva de recarga e a necessidade de informações claras sobre o reparo justificam medidas urgentes de transparência, que serão supridas com o cronograma. Advogado que defende a Abradecont, Rodrigo Raposo, celebrou a decisão parcial. “Objetivo principal passará a ser conclusão dos reparos e a obtenção da indenização dos cerca de 5.600 consumidores atingidos, em todo o país”. Recall do Volvo EX30 envolve risco na bateria A campanha foi iniciada em janeiro de 2026 e envolve unidades do Volvo EX30 produzidas entre 6 de setembro de 2024 e 25 de outubro de 2025. O problema identificado está relacionado a células da bateria de alta tensão. Uma falha no processo de fabricação pode provocar curto-circuito no interior dos módulos e elevar a temperatura do componente, com possibilidade de incêndio. Como medida preventiva, os proprietários dos veículos abrangidos foram orientados a limitar a recarga a 70% da capacidade da bateria até a realização dos procedimentos necessários. A recomendação reduz a possibilidade de utilização integral da autonomia e pode afetar a rotina de quem depende do veículo para deslocamentos mais longos. Cerca de 5,6 mil unidades foram comercializadas no Brasil, dentro de um universo superior a 40 mil veículos afetados globalmente. Relatos de proprietários apontam dificuldades para conseguir agendamento e falta de previsão para a substituição definitiva. Entre os problemas mencionados estão a indisponibilidade de componentes e a demora no retorno dos canais de atendimento. Em resposta à CNN Brasil, a Volvo Car informou que tomou conhecimento da determinação judicial e adotará as providências necessárias para cumpri-la. A empresa afirma que a campanha de recall já estava em andamento antes da ordem, com inspeções e eventual substituição dos componentes identificados como potencialmente afetados." "Campanha de recall já se encontrava em execução antes da decisão judicial, com a realização dos procedimentos de inspeção e eventual substituição dos componentes potencialmente afetados, em conformidade com as obrigações regulatórias aplicáveis e sob acompanhamento da Senacon. Os atendimentos seguem sendo realizados conforme a disponibilidade dos componentes necessários e a programação da rede autorizada", disse a montadora.

artigo.texto: Greenhouse gas emissions from industrial installations covered by the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) decreased by 3.3% in 2025 compared with the previous year. During the same period, revenue from emissions allowance auctions increased by 11% to EUR 43.2 billion. According to the European Commission’s 2026 Climate Action Progress Report and Carbon Market Report, published on 9 November, the iron and steel, cement, and chemical industries were the main contributors to the decrease in industrial emissions. While emissions decreased across most industrial sectors, emissions from the ceramics and aluminium industries increased by more than 2%. Total emissions covered by the ETS, including electricity and heat generation, industry, aviation, and maritime transport, decreased by 2% year on year to approximately 1.16 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. Emissions from electricity and heat generation decreased by 1.7%, while maritime transport emissions decreased by 4%. Aviation emissions, meanwhile, increased by 0.2%. EUR 23.9 billion in auction revenue allocated to member states Of the EUR 43.2 billion in auction revenue generated under the ETS in 2025, EUR 23.9 billion was allocated directly to EU member states. The Modernisation Fund received EUR 6.5 billion, the Innovation Fund EUR 2.6 billion, and the Social Climate Fund EUR 3.7 billion. This amount represents revenue generated from emissions allowance auctions, rather than the total trading volume of the carbon market. Commission stated that emissions reductions need to accelerate According to provisional data, the EU’s total net greenhouse gas emissions also decreased by 1.6% year on year in 2025. As a result, emissions were 39% below 1990 levels, while the EU economy grew by 74% over the same period. The Commission stated that the pace of emissions reductions had slowed compared with previous years and emphasized the need to accelerate reductions to meet the 2030 climate target. The EU aims to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 compared with 1990 levels. Author: SteelRadar Editorial Team

artigo.texto: Expansão de data centers nos EUA pode desacelerar após eleições legislativas | Vero NotíciasExpansão de data centers nos EUA pode desacelerar após eleições legislativas A expansão dos data centers de inteligência artificialnos Estados Unidos pode perder força após as eleições de meio de mandato, diante da pressão de democratas por restrições à construção de novas instalações. Entre as preocupações estão o elevado consumo de energia, o aumento das tarifas de eletricidade e os impactos ambientais. A senadora Elizabeth Warren defende uma moratória para novos empreendimentos. Analistas avaliam que possíveis restrições podem reduzir investimentos em inteligência artificial e pressionar ações de tecnologia na Nasdaq, enquanto os títulos públicos americanos ganham atratividade. Dados da CNN. O secretário de Comércio dos Estados Unidos, Howard Lutnick, enfrenta críticas de integrantes do governo Trump por sua relação com Jensen Huang, ex-CEO da Nvidia, e pela demora em restringir exportações de chips avançados à China. Autoridades questionam a decisão de não incluir a empresa Megaspeed, suspeita de repassar tecnologia americana ao mercado chinês, em uma lista de restrições comerciais. Os Correios registraram prejuízo de R$ 1,9 bilhão no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 19% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. Entre janeiro e setembro, as perdas acumuladas chegaram a R$ 7,48 bilhões, crescimento de 27%. A estatal atribui parte das dificuldades à queda nas receitas com encomendas e entregas internacionais, além do aumento de despesas judiciais e financeiras. O Brasil poderá receber até R$ 1 trilhão em investimentos em data centers até 2036, segundo estimativa da Associação Brasileira de Data Center (ABDC). O crescimento é impulsionado pela inteligência artificial, por incentivos fiscais e pela oferta de energia renovável. A Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) projeta que o setor responderá por cerca de 3% do consumo nacional de eletricidade em 2036, aumentando a necessidade de fontes capazes de garantir fornecimento contínuo. Cinco economistas avaliam que o ajuste fiscal do governo Lula, voltado a alcançar superávit de 0,5% do PIB em 2027, é insuficiente para conter o crescimento da dívida pública, próxima de 83% do PIB. Entre as propostas estão mudanças na correção do salário mínimo, revisão dos pisos de gastos com saúde e educação e maior controle das despesas obrigatórias. As medidas buscam estabilizar a dívida e abrir espaço para a redução dos juros. O presidente do Federal Reserve de Kansas City, Jeff Schmid, afirmou neste domingo (15) que a inflação nos Estados Unidos permanece acima da meta de 2% e apresenta uma trajetória preocupante. Durante uma conferência no Havaí, Schmid destacou que o banco central possui instrumentos para controlar a alta dos preços, mas não defendeu explicitamente novos aumentos dos juros.

artigo.texto: Last December, a Wythe County Board of Supervisors meeting was standing room only. Residents at the time said they were blindsided by the announcement of the first data center in the county, to be built on public land in an industrial park. The following year involved the announcement of a second, bigger data center on private land, sparking fears from local opponents that more were on the way. After an open house with one of the data center developers in October, many said they were still searching for answers. “Our ecosystems in Southwest Virginia are what make us so special,” said Maranda Edwards, a Wytheville resident, while at the open house. “We need to preserve that. People like looking out their windows and seeing the deer. With data centers, that’s going to go away, and that’s frustrating to know.” For Edwards and her family members, who live out in the county, zoning regulations could have shone light on plans for the data centers before they were a done deal, she said. Wythe County is one of a handful of localities in Virginia that has no zoning codes. Data centers — or any other development — can be built on private land without public notice or government intervention aside from state permitting in limited circumstances. As of early November, the process to put codes in place has been progressing at the urging of dozens of county residents who say they want the regulations to act as a deterrent for data center developers. Several said that as conservatives who otherwise wouldn’t want zoning implemented, they see a need for it in their community because of data centers. Across several counties in Southwest Virginia, a similar movement has taken root in meeting halls where officials have stressed the importance of getting specific data center zoning ordinances on the books. Most residents who speak at their public meetings have said they agree their localities need rules for data centers, though some are skeptical of their efficacy and have asked for multi-year moratoriums. No locality in Southwest Virginia has enacted a moratorium so far. For local governments, data centers can be a source of millions of dollars in property tax revenue, and some local officials have said they don’t want to write them off entirely. Wythe County zoning In early November, the Wythe County Planning Commission voted 5-2 to send its drafted ordinance and map for a board of supervisors public hearing, the next step in a process to get zoning codes on record. The commission recommended a July 1 implementation date. A vote on the ordinance and the map would occur after the public hearing, which hasn’t been scheduled yet. The process started several years ago before data centers became a major concern for people in Wythe County, according to Matt Hankins, deputy county administrator. At the time, it was another major type of development rankling residents: solar farms. In 2023, solar farm companies began building on hundreds of acres in the county, to the chagrin of residents around them, Hankins said in an interview. After looking at the options, he found the only way the county could make it possible to regulate solar farms on a local level was by enacting zoning codes. “We’ve had that conversation,” he said. “As part of it, residents said, ‘We’ve looked at zoning before. Come back to us with a light-touch ordinance that respects personal property rights and gives us some level of input and management over these projects as they come in.’” The data center issue is similar in nature to solar farms, he said, and has motivated groups of residents to advocate for zoning. The ordinance he and his team have worked on isn’t perfect, Hankins said, but it reflects the character of the county and the end goal of putting it in place, which is to ensure public input for major changes to the county’s landscape. The new codes would require a special exceptions permit for data centers, according to the draft document, which involves a public hearing and a vote from the board of supervisors. They would be allowed in commercial and industrial zones. Though some have called for a complete ban, Hankins said that it’s not legal to strike a particular use of private property from all areas of the county. The two data centers already in the works will also have to be grandfathered into the new codes, Hankins said. Wythe County residents have organized protests and spoken in droves at public meetings over the past year, asking for a way to halt the development of the data centers that have already been announced. They’ve voiced concerns over potential environmental impacts to the air and water, and the damage to their rural quality of life, if large-scale processing centers are built near their homes. At a public hearing hosted by the planning commission in late October, the majority of 17 people who spoke said they were in favor of zoning, specifically to protect the county from data centers. Those who were against zoning said they did not believe the codes would be protective enough against data centers to warrant restrictions on what they could do with their property. “Maybe we do need zoning to keep them out,” said Virginia Riggins, a county resident, during the October hearing. “But if they’re already here, it’s too late. Too little too late.” But for others, the possibility of Wythe County becoming a hotspot for dozens of data centers is the primary fear. Andrew Kegley has lived in the county for 46 years, he said in an interview. Like some, he believes the zoning has come too late, he said, but he is relieved it’s close to the finish line. He thinks it’s a dire need before other data center developers begin to see the county as a place to build without friction from the local government. He wants the effective date to be as soon as possible, he said. He advocated for Jan. 1 during the October hearing. “In an ideal world, we wouldn’t need zoning, nor would we be confronted with noxious developments like data centers

artigo.texto: Adding more bulk energy storage to New York’s grid will lower costs, optimise the generation and transmission of power, enhance energy grid infrastructure, and ensure the reliability and resilience of the State’s electricity system – all of which support the Governor’s Clean, Highly Affordable, Reliable Grid Expansion (CHARGE) agenda. “Today’s Bulk Energy Storage solicitation is another example of Governor Hochul’s commitment to meeting New York’s growing clean energy demand by putting affordability and reliability front and centre” said NYSERDA President and CEO Doreen M. Harris. “Energy storage reserves power when it is less expensive so that we can limit reliance on the most expensive power during peak hours – reducing the strain on our grid and delivering real cost savings to New Yorkers.” Administered by NYSERDA through its Bulk Energy Storage Programme, this competitive solicitation is open to a range of eligible energy storage technologies and seeks to achieve timely progress towards procuring three gigawatts of bulk energy storage over at least three annual solicitations in support of the state’s broader goal of deploying six gigawatts of energy storage by 2030. Any NYSERDA-supported energy storage project is contractually required to meet updated storage safety codes, which are among the most stringent in the nation, and reflect the work and recommendations of the New York State Inter-Agency Fire Safety Working Group convened by Governor Hochul in 2023. These safety codes ensure that first responders have the necessary training, facilities are sited safely, and that all sites have comprehensive emergency response plans. Entities interested in responding to this solicitation must first complete “Step One,” which is an initial qualifying step for proposers to demonstrate programme eligibility. Step One Eligibility Applications are due to NYSERDA by 3:00 p.m. ET on Thursday, December 15th, 2026. If NYSERDA deems proposals eligible, proposers will be invited to submit a “Step Two” bid proposal for project evaluation. NYSERDA’s Bulk Energy Storage Programme employs an Index Storage Credit (ISC) incentive, as established in the New York State Public Service Commission 2024 Energy Storage Order, modelled in part after the Renewable Energy Certificate and Offshore Wind Renewable Energy Credit utilised in other NYSERDA programmes. NYSERDA supports robust safety measures for all projects and, as a result, will not pay for ISCs until the awarded and contracted projects are permitted, installed and operating and have passed their peer review process and quality assurance inspection – both key milestones to ensure that all projects are designed and constructed with New York’s best-in-class safety standards. Project proposals must include plans to comply with the State’s comprehensive safety and security requirements, and to comply with the Bulk Energy Storage Programme Manual requirements. Also, associated with this solicitation, NY Green Bank (NYGB), a division of NYSERDA and a specialised investment fund dedicated to bridging financial gaps in clean energy and renewable infrastructure markets in New York State, is prepared to support project developers and investors with a range of financing options in order to advance energy storage. Entities interested in applying for this financing can submit an application to NYGB RFP No. 1. NYSERDA’s siting team also works closely with local governments to provide tailored education, technical assistance, and model local laws. Through its clean energy siting resources, the siting team empowers communities with the tools and knowledge to make informed decisions and manage responsible clean energy development in host communities. “Battery storage can help lower costs for consumers by making better use of the existing electric grid, reducing wasted renewable energy, providing extra power when demand is highest and potentially eliminating the need for costly new transmission lines” added Secretary of State Walter Mosley. “Adding more bulk energy storage to New York’s grid will lower costs and enhance energy grid infrastructure and that’s why we applaud the Governor’s ongoing commitment to protecting New York’s energy consumers, while moving us closer to the state’s energy goals.” New York’s 6 GW Energy Storage Roadmap, created to support the state’s target of 6 gigawatts deployed by 2030, recommended deployment of an incremental 4,700 megawatts consisting of 3,000 megawatts bulk, 200 megawatts of new residential-scale energy storage and 1,500 megawatts of new commercial and community-scale energy. Additionally, at least 35 percent of off-site retail and bulk energy storage projects supported by NYSERDA are planned to be sited in downstate New York, where they are most likely to benefit disadvantaged communities and reduce peaker plant emissions. The announcement builds on awards recently announced by NYSERDA through its first Bulk Energy Storage solicitation. The eight contracted bulk energy storage projects, which range geographically from New York City and Long Island to Hudson Valley and Western New York, will add 950 megawatts of new energy storage capacity once operational. The Clean, Highly Affordable, Reliable Grid Expansion (CHARGE) agenda is a comprehensive plan to keep the lights on and costs down for New Yorkers while achieving a reliable, zero-emission grid. The five-pronged strategy focuses on driving down consumer costs, holding energy companies accountable, building clean energy at scale, modernising the state's aging grid, and growing a clean economy with family-sustaining jobs. Through bold initiatives like the Ratepayer Protection Plan, historic transmission buildouts, and a new 8.4-gigawatt "Nuclear Backbone," the CHARGE agenda ensures an affordable, resilient, and self-sufficient energy future that prioritises everyday ratepayers while building a cleaner, more sustainable New York.
